payload.title: Count of the Levite families

aliases: the God of our Lord Jesus Christ
him who sits on the throne
payload.name: God / Yahweh, the Father and God of Israel
payload.note: The one God, creator and speaker of the Old Testament and the Father of Jesus Christ in the New Testament; distinct from Jesus in every entry.

stages.label: God the Father (radiance and cloud)

quotes.quote: Heaven is my throne, and the earth is my footstool.
Behold, Yahweh rides on a swift cloud, and comes to Egypt.

stages.text: God the Father: no human face or body; presence shown only as radiance, cloud and fire. A brilliant white-gold light without a source, veiled by a dense, slowly moving cloud, with a fire-like glow at its heart. Throne-light and footstool-earth implied at the edges, never a figure seated in it.

payload.name: Moses
payload.note: Israel's lawgiver and leader who led the people out of Egypt, received the law at Sinai and is named across the Old and New Testament divisions as the same individual, distinguished only by the sections in which he appears or is mentioned.

stages.label: Moses, elder

quotes.quote: Moses was eighty years old, and Aaron eighty-three years old, when they spoke to Pharaoh.

stages.text: Moses: an old man of about eighty; lean, weathered build; brown skin darkened by desert sun; white hair and a long white beard; deep-set, steady eyes and lined brow; a plain undyed linen tunic belted at the waist with a long dark-brown wool cloak; he carries a wooden shepherd's staff of dark acacia wood, and only he bears the rod of God.

stages.label: Moses, infant

quotes.quote: The woman conceived and bore a son. When she saw that he was a fine child, she hid him three months.

stages.text: Moses: a newborn infant; soft smooth skin; a small round face; a little dark hair; wrapped in plain linen cloth and laid in a woven reed basket sealed with bitumen and pitch; no beard, no staff, no adult clothing.

stages.label: Moses, adult

quotes.quote: But when he was forty years old, it came into his heart to visit his brothers, the children of Israel.

stages.text: Moses: a man of about forty; lean, strong, well-proportioned build; brown skin; short dark hair and a close-trimmed dark beard; alert, sober face; a knee-length undyed linen tunic with a dark woven wool cloak of brown and grey pinned at the shoulder; he carries a plain wooden shepherd's staff.

payload.name: Aaron, brother of Moses
payload.note: Moses' older brother and first high priest, in Exodus and in Numbers (census, offerings, death on Mount Hor); the same man across both divisions.

stages.label: Aaron, the first high priest

quotes.quote: Amram took Jochebed his father’s sister to himself as wife; and she bore him Aaron and Moses.
Of the blue, purple, and scarlet, they made finely worked garments for ministering in the holy place, and made the holy garments for Aaron
Aaron cast down his rod before Pharaoh and before his servants, and it became a serpent.

stages.text: Aaron: man in his eighties, older brother of Moses; lean, upright build; olive-brown skin; short grey-streaked beard and close-cropped hair; calm, grave face with deep-set eyes. Signature outfit: a long white linen tunic with a blue robe, a woven ephod of blue, purple and scarlet, a breastplate, and a linen headband. Props: none carried alone; the rod of the Exodus is sometimes held.

payload.name: The Levites
payload.note: The tribe of Levi serving in the tabernacle and carrying its furnishings in Numbers.

stages.label: The Levites

quotes.quote: The Levites purified themselves from sin, and they washed their clothes
from twenty-five years old and upward they shall go in to wait on the service
They shall carry the tabernacle and all its furnishings

stages.text: The Levites: men from twenty-five years old upward, of mature working age; sturdy, unhurried build from carrying the tabernacle frames and furnishings; olive-brown skin; short dark hair and close-trimmed beard; calm, dignified features. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic belted at the waist with a cloak of undyed wool, washed clean; a wooden carrying pole across the shoulders.

aliases: the mountain that might be touched
payload.name: Horeb/Mount Sinai
payload.note: The single mountain of God where the law and covenant are given; all listed entries (Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers, Deuteronomy, 1 Kings, Malachi, Hebrews) refer to the same mountain under the names Horeb, Sinai, God's mountain, referenced across divisions.

stages.label: Horeb/Mount Sinai

quotes.quote: All of Mount Sinai smoked, because Yahweh descended on it in fire
You shall set bounds to the people all around
the cloud covered it six days
The mountain burned with fire to the heart of the sky, with darkness, cloud, and thick darkness.

stages.text: Horeb/Mount Sinai: a single steep granite mountain rising from a stark desert wilderness of rock and sand; its lower slopes are broken boulders and gravel, its upper peak sharp and dark, with a cloud-wrapped summit. The base is marked by a rocky plain where the people camp, bounded by stones. No vegetation beyond scattered desert shrub; the mountain has no buildings.

aliases: the door of the Tent of Meeting
the court of the Tent of Meeting
payload.name: the tabernacle (portable sanctuary)
payload.note: The one portable sanctuary of the wilderness, described in Exodus 25-40 and referred to as the Tent of Meeting in Leviticus and Numbers; all three entries are the same place.

stages.label: The tabernacle (portable sanctuary)

quotes.quote: made the tabernacle with ten curtains of fine twined linen, blue, purple, and scarlet. They made them with cherubim
He made curtains of goats’ hair for a covering over the tabernacle.
He made the boards for the tabernacle, twenty boards for the south side southward.
the sockets around the court, the sockets of the gate of the court, all the pins of the tabernacle

stages.text: The tabernacle: a portable sanctuary of a rectangular tent of fine twined linen curtains in blue, purple and scarlet woven with cherubim, over a covering of goats' hair and rams' skins, stretched over upright acacia boards overlaid with gold, set in silver sockets and held by gold-covered bars, enclosed by a court of white linen hangings on bronze pillars.

payload.title: Anointing at Simon the Pharisee's house

aliases: the apostle and high priest of our confession
the great shepherd of the sheep
the author and perfecter of faith
the mediator of a new covenant
the Lion of the tribe of Judah
the rider called Faithful and True
KING OF KINGS AND LORD OF LORDS
payload.name: Jesus Christ, the Son of God and Lord
payload.note: The one Jesus: the teacher from Nazareth of the Gospels and Acts, and the risen, exalted Christ and Lord of the epistles and Revelation; the same individual across all divisions, with death, resurrection and changed portrayal not creating new individuals.

stages.label: Adult Jesus

quotes.quote: Jesus himself, when he began to teach, was about thirty years old, being the son (as was supposed) of Joseph, the son of Heli,

stages.text: Jesus: man of about thirty, lean and strong from carpentry and walking; olive-brown skin; dark brown shoulder-length hair parted at centre; short dark beard; calm dark eyes; wears a plain undyed tunic of natural linen with a dark blue-grey cloak and sandals; carries no props except a shepherd's staff when a scene calls for one.

stages.label: Infant Jesus

quotes.quote: She gave birth to her firstborn son. She wrapped him in bands of cloth and laid him in a feeding trough, because there was no room for them in the inn.

stages.text: Jesus: newborn to about two years old; olive-brown skin, a little dark hair and dark eyes; a small infant or toddler's build, no beard. Plain undyed swaddling linen for the newborn; a small plain linen tunic as a toddler. No adult clothing or props.

stages.label: Boy Jesus

quotes.quote: When he was twelve years old, they went up to Jerusalem according to the custom of the feast;

stages.text: Jesus: boy of about twelve, slim and sturdy; olive-brown skin; dark brown hair cut short at the neck; dark eyes; no beard; wears a plain undyed tunic of natural linen with a dark blue-grey cloak; no props.

payload.name: Simon the Pharisee
payload.note: Pharisee host at whose house Jesus is anointed in Luke 7; explicitly not Simon Peter and not the leper of Bethany.

stages.label: Simon the Pharisee
stages.text: Simon the Pharisee: a man in his fifties, of middling height and sturdy build. Olive-brown skin, close-cut dark hair streaked with grey, and a neatly trimmed grey beard. Lined, serious face with dignity and reserve. Signature outfit: a long undertunic of undyed cream linen under a deep blue wool cloak with blue tassels at the hem. Carries no props.

aliases: a woman of the city who was a sinner
payload.name: The sinful woman
payload.note: Woman of the city who anoints Jesus' feet at Simon the Pharisee's house in Luke 7; distinguished from the Bethany woman by setting and by being called a sinner.

stages.label: The sinful woman
stages.text: The sinful woman: a woman of about thirty, slender and modest in build, with olive skin and dark brown hair worn long and loose, partly veiled by a dusty ochre head covering. Her face is grave and tender, with dark eyes. Her signature outfit is a plain undyed linen tunic of ochre-brown beneath a deep indigo cloak. She carries a small alabaster flask of ointment.

payload.name: Capernaum
payload.note: The lakeside town in Galilee where Jesus lives, teaches and heals, with a synagogue and Simon Peter's house; all four Gospels' entries describe this one place.

stages.label: Capernaum

quotes.quote: Leaving Nazareth, he came and lived in Capernaum, which is by the sea, in the region of Zebulun and Naphtali
They went into Capernaum, and immediately on the Sabbath day he entered into the synagogue and taught.
They entered into the boat, and were going over the sea to Capernaum.

stages.text: Capernaum: a fishing town of plain basalt and limestone houses with flat roofs, packed close along a curving shore of the Sea of Galilee. A white limestone synagogue with a tall carved doorway stands near the water, its pillars facing the lake. Nearby, a modest family house of stone with a courtyard and reed-thatched roof marks Simon's home. Fishing boats are drawn up on the stones, nets hung on poles. Olive trees, palms and fig trees grow on the slopes behind the town, with dry hills rising beyond.

payload.title: Thanksgiving for the Colossians' faith

aliases: my child's father in the faith
the aged prisoner of Christ Jesus
payload.name: Paul the apostle
payload.note: The apostle Paul, author and speaker of all thirteen letters; the same individual across Romans, Corinthians, Galatians, Ephesians, Philippians, Colossians, Thessalonians, Timothy, Titus and Philemon, identified by his apostolic authorship and first-person voice.

stages.label: Paul the apostle

quotes.quote: being such a one as Paul, the aged, but also a prisoner of Jesus Christ.
I, Paul, write this greeting with my own hand. Remember my chains.
I, Paul, write this with my own hand

stages.text: Paul the apostle: man of middle to later years, perhaps fifties to sixties, wiry and weathered from travel and imprisonment; Jewish Mediterranean features, olive-brown skin, short greying-dark beard and close-cropped hair receding at the temples; lined brow, steady dark eyes. Signature outfit: plain undyed wool tunic in ochre-brown under a dark-blue cloak. Signature prop: a rolled parchment scroll and a reed pen case at the belt.

payload.name: Timothy
payload.note: Paul's young companion and fellow worker, the son of Eunice from Lystra, who appears in Acts, the letters co-sent with Paul, and the two pastoral letters addressed to him; all twelve entries are the same man.

stages.label: Timothy

quotes.quote: a certain disciple was there, named Timothy, the son of a Jewess who believed, but his father was a Greek.

stages.text: Timothy: a young man of about twenty to twenty-five; slender, medium build; olive-brown skin; short dark curly hair and a smooth, clean-shaven face; calm, earnest features. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic with a dark brown woollen cloak. He carries a traveller's leather satchel and walking staff.

aliases: the saints and faithful brothers in Christ at Colossae
payload.name: The saints at Colossae
payload.note: The Christian community addressed in the letter to the Colossians; addressed rather than acting on stage.

stages.label: The saints at Colossae

quotes.quote: to the saints and faithful brothers in Christ at Colossae

stages.text: The saints at Colossae: a typical member is an adult of working age, thirty to fifty, sturdy and weathered from labour in the fields and markets of the Lycus valley. Olive to warm brown skin, dark hair cut short or tied back, a trimmed beard on men, a modest head covering on women. Calm, steady, dignified face. Plain undyed linen or wool tunic with a earth-toned cloak in ochre, grey or dull blue.

payload.name: Colossae
payload.note: City in Phrygia whose believers receive the letter.

stages.label: Colossae

quotes.quote: to the saints and faithful brothers in Christ at Colossae

stages.text: Colossae: a Roman-era city in the Lycus valley of Phrygia, western Anatolia. Low stone and mudbrick houses with flat roofs stand on a terrace above a green river plain. Olive, fig and vine grow in the orchards beyond the walls, and white limestone cliffs rise to the south. A stone theatre and a modest civic building mark the town centre, and a small house-church of plastered stone stands among the courtyard dwellings.

payload.title: Pharaoh's dreams and the cup bearer's remembrance

payload.name: Pharaoh of Joseph
payload.note: Egyptian king of Joseph's era who dreams of cattle and grain and elevates Joseph; the king who knew Joseph, distinct from the Exodus oppressor.

stages.label: Pharaoh of Joseph

quotes.quote: Pharaoh took off his signet ring from his hand, and put it on Joseph’s hand, and arrayed him in robes of fine linen, and put a gold chain about his neck.

stages.text: Pharaoh of Joseph: man in his fifties; broad, dignified build; deep bronze skin; close-cropped dark hair under a tall blue and gold royal headcloth with a cobra emblem; neatly trimmed beard, ceremonial false beard; calm, grave face. Signature outfit: white pleated linen kilt and shendyt with a broad golden collar in blue and gold. Props: gold signet ring, gold chain, crook and flail of office.

payload.name: the chief cup bearer
payload.note: Pharaoh's cupbearer imprisoned with Joseph, restored to office, forgets Joseph for a time.

stages.label: The chief cup bearer

quotes.quote: the butler of the king of Egypt and his baker offended their lord, the king of Egypt.
The chief cup bearer told his dream to Joseph, and said to him, “In my dream, behold, a vine was in front of me,
He restored the chief cup bearer to his position again, and he gave the cup into Pharaoh’s hand;

stages.text: The chief cup bearer: a man in his middle years, lean and upright, with dark brown skin, short-cropped black hair and a clean-shaven face, a calm and watchful look. He wears a pleated white linen kilt and a short linen tunic, with a broad collar of blue and gold beads at the neck, and carries a gold cup.

payload.name: Egypt's magicians and wise men
payload.note: The Egyptian magicians of Pharaoh's court in Genesis who fail to interpret the dreams; distinguished from the Egyptian people at large and from the Chaldean wise men of Babylon.

stages.label: Egypt's magicians and wise men

quotes.quote: I told it to the magicians, but there was no one who could explain it to me.

stages.text: Egypt's magicians and wise men: middle-aged to elderly court scholars; lean, dignified build; warm brown skin; close-cropped hair and a neatly trimmed beard; calm, intent facial features. Signature outfit: a pleated white linen kilt and wrap with a blue-and-gold collar, worn with sandals. Signature prop: a papyrus scroll case.

payload.name: Pharaoh's house
payload.note: Royal residence and court of Pharaoh in Genesis where dreams are told and Joseph is brought before the king; distinct from the other courts in this group.

stages.label: Pharaoh's house
stages.text: Pharaoh's house: royal palace of mud-brick and limestone on a raised terrace above the Nile floodplain; tall painted pylon gateway, columned hall with papyrus-bud capitals, shaded courtyards, cool stone floors; date palms, sycamores and green reeds along the river edge; the great river and irrigated fields visible beyond the walls.

payload.title: Meditation on the law (remaining stanzas)

aliases: the anointed of the God of Jacob
payload.name: David son of Jesse (king of Israel)
payload.note: The single David of the Hebrew books and the New Testament references: son of Jesse, shepherd, harpist, anointed king, father of Solomon; all entries describe this one king and the hint's second David is not needed.

stages.label: David as king

quotes.quote: David was thirty years old when he began to reign, and he reigned forty years.

stages.text: David: a man of about thirty to fifty, athletic and broad-shouldered, of medium height; ruddy complexion, bright dark eyes, short dark beard trimmed close; dark hair cut to the shoulder. Signature outfit: a long blue royal robe with a sash of crimson and gold, over an undertunic of white linen. Carries a bronze-bossed sword in a leather scabbard and a harp.

stages.label: David as youth

quotes.quote: He sent, and brought him in. Now he was ruddy, with a handsome face and good appearance. Yahweh said, “Arise! Anoint him, for this is he.”

stages.text: David: a beardless youth and young adult before kingship; slender, wiry build, ruddy complexion, bright dark eyes and short dark curly hair. Plain undyed brown wool tunic, leather belt and sandals; shepherd's pouch and sling when called for. No crown or royal robes.

stages.label: David as elder

quotes.quote: Now King David was old and advanced in years; and they covered him with clothes, but he couldn’t keep warm.

stages.text: David: an old man of about seventy, lean and bent with age, his frame still dignified; ruddy complexion faded to a weathered warmth, dark eyes deep-set and gentle, white hair and a white beard cut short. Signature outfit: a plain long wool robe of undyed cream with a dark blue cloak over the shoulders for warmth. Carries a staff of almond wood.

payload.title: Intercession refused and Jeremiah's lament

payload.name: Jeremiah son of Hilkiah
payload.note: Prophet from Anathoth who speaks most of the book.

stages.label: Jeremiah

quotes.quote: The words of Jeremiah the son of Hilkiah, one of the priests who were in Anathoth in the land of Benjamin.
They let down Jeremiah with cords. In the dungeon there was no water, but mire; and Jeremiah sank in the mire.

stages.text: Jeremiah: a man in his middle years, lean and weathered from long journeys and imprisonment, with a grave, careworn face and deep-set dark eyes. Close-cropped dark hair and a short greying beard. Dark-skinned Levantine complexion. Wears a plain undyed linen priestly tunic under a long brown wool cloak, the cloak worn thin at the hem. Carries a plain wooden staff.

aliases: the city of my fathers' tombs
payload.name: Jerusalem
payload.note: The capital city of Judah (also called Jebus, David's city, the holy city, Zion as city in some books); the city itself, distinct from the hill/mountain of Zion as a place of Yahweh's dwelling.

stages.label: Jerusalem

quotes.quote: they buried him in David's city
a breach was made in the city

stages.text: Jerusalem: a walled city on a steep limestone ridge of the Judean hills, terraces of olive and fig trees falling into deep valleys. Stone and mud-brick houses with flat roofs crowd the slopes; a fortified citadel of the stronghold of Zion stands on the high ground. Massive city walls with gates, and above the city the temple mount crowned by a stone-built temple of Yahweh.

payload.title: Samson, Delilah and the temple of Dagon

payload.name: Samson
payload.note: Nazirite judge of Dan whose exploits against the Philistines include the riddle, the foxes, the jawbone, and the temple of Dagon.

stages.label: Samson

quotes.quote: No razor shall come on his head, for the child shall be a Nazirite to God from the womb.
The woman bore a son and named him Samson. The child grew, and Yahweh blessed him.
No razor has ever come on my head; for I have been a Nazirite to God from my mother’s womb.

stages.text: Samson: a strong man in his prime, roughly thirty years old, broad-shouldered and powerfully muscled with a lean, weathered frame; sun-browned olive skin; long, uncut hair falling past his shoulders, dark brown, and a full untrimmed beard; a grave, dignified face with a strong nose and deep-set eyes. Signature outfit: a woven undyed linen tunic in ochre with a plain brown wool cloak. Signature prop: none he carries; his only sign is the unshorn hair.

aliases: woman of the valley of Sorek
payload.name: Delilah
payload.note: Woman of the valley of Sorek who learns the secret of Samson's strength for the Philistine lords.

stages.label: Delilah

quotes.quote: he loved a woman in the valley of Sorek, whose name was Delilah.

stages.text: Delilah: a woman of about thirty, slender and upright, with warm olive-brown skin. Dark hair, long and braided, falls over one shoulder with fine linen threads bound into the braid. Clear, watchful eyes, a straight nose and a composed mouth. Her signature outfit is a long woven tunic of deep indigo with a dull ochre cloak drawn over the shoulders. Carries a small woven basket of wool.

payload.name: Philistines
payload.note: The oppressors of Israel and lords of the Philistines in Samson's story; a foreign people, not an Israelite tribe.

stages.label: Philistines (typical warrior of the lords' armies)

quotes.quote: the five lords of the Philistines
thirty thousand chariots, six thousand horsemen

stages.text: Philistines: adult men of the coastal cities, age twenty to forty; medium-to-broad build, sun-browned skin; close-cropped dark hair and a short beard; calm, hard-set features, not caricatured. Typical dress: a knee-length woven tunic of undyed wool with a bordered hem in blue or red, a leather belt and a short cloak of dark wool. Signature props: a bronze helmet with a crest and a round shield, carried by the army; no props carried by the figure alone.

payload.name: Gaza (Philistine city in Judges)
payload.note: The Philistine city where Samson carries off the gates and is imprisoned and grinds at the mill; the same city as the Gaza judged in Amos.

stages.label: Gaza

quotes.quote: they brought him down to Gaza and bound him with fetters of bronze; and he ground at the mill in the prison.
The lords of the Philistines gathered together to offer a great sacrifice to Dagon their god
I will send a fire on the wall of Gaza, and it will devour its palaces.

stages.text: Gaza: a fortified coastal city on a low sandy ridge above the Mediterranean, with thick mudbrick and stone city walls and tall gates of heavy timber bound with bronze. Within the walls stand flat-roofed houses, palaces of dressed stone, and a great temple of Dagon with columns of wood supporting a broad roof. Sparse palms, olive trees and tamarisk grow near the sand dunes.

payload.name: Valley of Sorek
payload.note: Place where Delilah lives, near the setting of Samson's downfall; distinct from any other valley in the group.

stages.label: Valley of Sorek

quotes.quote: he loved a woman in the valley of Sorek, whose name was Delilah

stages.text: Valley of Sorek: a broad, fertile valley of the Shephelah lowlands between Israelite hill country and Philistine plain, its slopes terraced with vines and olive trees, grain fields gold in season, sycamores by a seasonal stream. Mud-brick and fieldstone village houses with flat roofs cluster on the lower ridges, and a fortified town walls the valley mouth.

payload.name: Temple of Dagon in Gaza
payload.note: Philistine temple in Gaza where Samson pulls down the pillars; a pagan temple, unlike Yahweh's houses elsewhere in the group.

stages.label: Temple of Dagon in Gaza

quotes.quote: went into the house of their god and ate and drank

stages.text: Temple of Dagon in Gaza: a large roofed hall of dressed limestone and mudbrick set within a fortified Philistine town; a broad forecourt paved with flat stones; great central wooden pillars of cedar on stone bases supporting a flat roof crowded with the people of the town; a stepped platform before the entrance; dry scrub and a few olive trees beyond the walls under pale sky.

payload.title: Destruction of Jerusalem and exile

payload.name: Nebuchadnezzar
payload.note: King of Babylon who conquers Jerusalem and destroys the temple; recurs across Kings, Chronicles, Jeremiah, Ezekiel and Daniel.

stages.label: Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon

quotes.quote: the king of Babylon had taken, from the brook of Egypt to the river Euphrates
King Nebuchadnezzar fell on his face, worshiped Daniel

stages.text: Nebuchadnezzar: a mature man in his forties to fifties; broad, strong build; olive-bronze skin; dark hair and a full, carefully curled beard in Babylonian royal style; a broad, dignified face with heavy-lidded eyes. Signature outfit: a long crimson and gold court robe over a white linen tunic, with a tall royal crown of gold and lapis. Carries a gold-headed staff of office.

aliases: the king of the Chaldeans's army
payload.name: Chaldeans
payload.note: Babylonian army that destroys Jerusalem and the temple.

stages.label: Chaldeans

quotes.quote: the Chaldeans, that bitter and hasty nation who march through the width of the earth
who killed their young men with the sword in the house of their sanctuary

stages.text: Chaldeans: adult soldiers of the Babylonian army, lean and hardened, from young men to middle age; sun-darkened skin of the Mesopotamian plain; close-cropped or short-bearded dark hair and beard, strong brows, a stern and weary face. Signature outfit: a knee-length tunic of dark wool with a bronze scale or lamellar coat over it, a conical or round helmet, colours of ochre, bronze and deep red. Signature prop: a curved or straight short sword at the hip.

payload.name: Babylon
payload.note: The city and empire of exile and captivity across the prophets, histories and psalms, also called Babylonia, Shinar and the land of the Chaldeans; the same place in every division.

stages.label: Babylon

quotes.quote: The wide walls of Babylon will be utterly overthrown. Her high gates will be burned with fire.
I will execute judgment on Bel in Babylon, and I will bring out of his mouth that which he has swallowed up.
He brought the vessels into the treasure house of his god.
I will record Rahab and Babylon among those who acknowledge me.

stages.text: Babylon: a vast walled city of baked brick on a flat plain watered by broad canals and rivers, its wide walls rising high and its great gates of bronze-banded cedar. Date palms and reed beds line the riverbanks, and ziggurat towers and palace roofs of brick rise above the flat skyline, with the temple of Bel among them.

payload.title: Recital of the patriarchs and the Exodus

aliases: those who came out of Egypt
payload.name: The Israelite people (the children of Israel)
payload.note: The collective Israelite nation across Exodus through Malachi and Hebrews, one body whose different portrayals (marching nation, assembly, covenant people, judged northern kingdom, returned community, wilderness generation) are all the same people; distinguish only from the returned community of Nehemiah in the note by the Judah/Jerusalem setting, but these are the same people.

stages.label: The Israelite people

quotes.quote: Now these are the names of the sons of Israel, who came into Egypt
You shall tell the children of Israel this
So they shall put my name on the children of Israel; and I will bless them.

stages.text: The Israelite people: a typical member is an adult of mixed age, from youth to middle years, of sturdy and weathered build shaped by desert travel and field labour. Skin is warm olive-brown, hair dark and kept short or tied back, with full beards on men. Faces are calm and steady with dark eyes. Signature outfit: a plain undyed woven linen tunic in ochre or cream with a wool cloak in earth brown.

payload.name: Egypt
payload.note: The land of Egypt where patriarchs sojourn, Israel is enslaved and plagues fall; recurs in Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers, Psalms, Ezekiel, Hosea, Micah and Hebrews as the same land.

stages.label: Egypt

quotes.quote: The land of Egypt is before you. Make your father and your brothers dwell in the best of the land.
Israel lived in the land of Egypt, in the land of Goshen
But the midwives feared God, and didn’t do what the king of Egypt commanded them
for Memphis will become a desolation, and will be burned up, without inhabitant.

stages.text: Egypt: a long green valley of the Nile flanked by pale desert; broad river channels, canals and reed marsh; fertile black earth fields of barley and flax; date palms and sycamores; mud-brick and limestone cities with tall temple pylons, obelisks and fortified walls; the Delta with its towns of Goshen and Zoan.

payload.title: Warning about Herod; lament over Jerusalem

payload.name: the Pharisees
payload.note: The Pharisees as a religious party opposing Jesus over Sabbath, purity, tradition and table fellowship; all four Gospel entries describe this same party, so they form one cluster.

stages.label: the Pharisees

quotes.quote: The scribes and the Pharisees sit on Moses’ seat.
like whitened tombs, which outwardly appear beautiful

stages.text: The Pharisees: a typical member of the party is a man of middle age to elderly, with a lean, serious build; olive skin weathered by travel; a close-cut or short-bearded face with a grave, watchful expression; hair kept neatly under a head covering. Signature outfit: a long white linen tunic with a dark blue-violet cloak and tassel fringes at the corners. Signature prop: a small phylactery box on the forehead and forearm, and a scroll of the law.

payload.name: Galilee
payload.note: The northern region of Galilee where Jesus preaches, teaches and heals; both Matthew and Luke describe the same region, so these entries are one place.

stages.label: Galilee

quotes.quote: Walking by the sea of Galilee, he saw two brothers
teaching in their synagogues, preaching the Good News of the Kingdom
toward the sea, beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles

stages.text: Galilee: Northern hill country falling to a freshwater lake, the sea of Galilee, its shore lined with fishing boats and nets drying on stone. Low limestone villages of flat-roofed houses, a white stone synagogue with a shallow portico, terraced olive groves, fig trees and scrubland. Roman roads and a distant Gentile town on the slopes.

payload.title: The Egyptian guide and the rescue

payload.name: the Egyptian servant
payload.note: Unnamed sick Egyptian servant of an Amalekite who guides David to the raiders in 1 Samuel. Distinct from Hagar, the Egyptian servant of Sarai in Genesis.

stages.label: The Egyptian servant
stages.text: The Egyptian servant: a young man of about twenty, lean and worn by hunger and fever, with dark brown skin, close-cropped black hair and a short unkempt beard. Weathered face, sunken cheeks, and tired dark eyes. He wears a plain undyed linen tunic belted with cord, and a faded brown cloak. He carries a leather water skin.

payload.name: Amalekites
payload.note: The Amalekite people, an enemy nation that attacks Israel at Rephidim in Exodus, comes against Israel at Hormah in Numbers, and is recalled in Deuteronomy as the nation that struck Israel's weary rear; all three refer to the same people.

stages.label: Amalekites

quotes.quote: Then Amalek came and fought with Israel in Rephidim.
the Amalekites had made a raid on the South and on Ziklag, and had struck Ziklag and burned it with fire

stages.text: Amalekites: a typical warrior of a desert people, adult, aged roughly twenty-five to forty; lean, weathered build; sun-darkened olive-brown skin; dark hair tied back, short beard kept close; strong, wind-creased face with a steady gaze. Signature outfit: a long undyed linen tunic belted with leather, over it a sand-coloured woven cloak in ochre and brown. Carries a curved sword at the belt and a leather shield as their own props.

payload.name: Ziklag
payload.note: The single town of Ziklag in the southern Judah region, given to David by Achish, raided by Amalekites, and a refuge for David; all three entries describe the same place, so they form one cluster.

stages.label: Ziklag

quotes.quote: Then Achish gave him Ziklag that day: therefore Ziklag belongs to the kings of Judah to this day.
the Amalekites had made a raid on the South and on Ziklag, and had struck Ziklag and burned it with fire

stages.text: Ziklag: a fortified town on a low rise in the southern hill country of Judah, the Negev edge. Mudbrick and fieldstone houses with flat roofs cluster behind a stout gate of timber and stone. Dry terraces, olive trees, vines and scrub of terebinth; wadi beds nearby, pale and dusty under sun.

payload.title: Thanksgiving of the redeemed

payload.name: The righteous (Psalms)
payload.note: The collective of the godly and humble who trust Yahweh and suffer oppression across the Psalms; distinct from the remnant of Judah, which is a specific Judahite community addressed by Zephaniah.

stages.label: The righteous (Psalms)

quotes.quote: My shield is with God, who saves the upright in heart.
For the needy shall not always be forgotten, nor the hope of the poor perish forever.
He raises up the poor out of the dust, and lifts up the needy from the ash heap,

stages.text: The righteous: adults of mixed age, mostly middle-aged, lean and sturdy from farm and road labour; olive to brown skin; dark hair kept short or tied back, men with trimmed beards; plain, careworn faces, dignified and steady. Signature outfit: undyed linen or wool tunic in ochre and earth tones with a plain brown woollen cloak. Signature prop: a simple staff or walking stick.

payload.name: The wilderness (Exodus route)
payload.note: The desert stretches Israel travels from Egypt through Shur, Sin and Marah, with manna, quail and water miracles; the same wilderness as the Psalms and Amos references.

stages.label: The wilderness (Exodus route)

quotes.quote: they went out into the wilderness of Shur; and they went three days in the wilderness, and found no water.
on the surface of the wilderness was a small round thing, small as the frost on the ground.
in a dry and weary land, where there is no water.

stages.text: The wilderness: a vast arid tableland of pale sand, gravel plains and dark rock outcrops rising to bare mountains, scattered with thorn scrub and sparse grasses in the wadis. Tents and camp-circles mark the encampments; a distant mountain, Sinai, rises above the plain. Dry riverbeds, stone wells and rock fissures suggest hidden water.

payload.title: Earth swallows the rebels; fire consumes the 250

payload.name: Korah
payload.note: Levite, son of Izhar, who leads the rebellion against Moses and Aaron.

stages.label: Korah

quotes.quote: Now Korah, the son of Izhar, the son of Kohath, the son of Levi
have Korah and all his company take censers

stages.text: Korah: a man in his middle years, lean and sturdy, with weathered brown skin, a dark beard trimmed short, and deep-set, intent eyes. He wears a woven undyed linen tunic with a deep indigo cloak over it, and a Levite's plain belt of braided cord. His signature prop is a bronze censer held in his hand.

payload.name: Dathan
payload.note: Reubenite, son of Eliab, who rebels with Korah and dies when the earth opens.

stages.label: Dathan

quotes.quote: Now Korah, the son of Izhar, the son of Kohath, the son of Levi, with Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab
Dathan and Abiram came out, and stood at the door of their tents with their wives, their sons, and their little ones.

stages.text: Dathan: a man of middle years, sturdy and weathered from desert travel; olive-brown skin; dark hair and a short trimmed beard streaked with grey; a lined, proud, unyielding face. Signature outfit: a woven undertunic of undyed linen under a deep rust-red wool cloak with a Reubenite fringe at the hem.

payload.name: Abiram
payload.note: Reubenite, son of Eliab, who rebels with Korah and dies when the earth opens.

stages.label: Abiram

quotes.quote: Now Korah, the son of Izhar, the son of Kohath, the son of Levi, with Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab
Dathan and Abiram came out, and stood at the door of their tents with their wives, their sons, and their little ones.

stages.text: Abiram: a man in his middle years, mature and sturdy of build, with weathered brown skin from desert travel. Short dark hair and a full, close-cut beard greying at the chin. Deep-set, steady eyes and a lined brow. Signature outfit: a plain undyed woven linen tunic under an earth-brown wool cloak with fringed hem. He carries a plain wooden staff.

payload.title: Closing of Hezekiah and Manasseh's idolatry

payload.name: Manasseh
payload.note: Judean king who restores idolatry.

stages.label: Manasseh, king of Judah

quotes.quote: Manasseh was twelve years old when he began to reign, and he reigned fifty-five years in Jerusalem.
who took Manasseh in chains, bound him with fetters, and carried him to Babylon.

stages.text: Manasseh: man of mature age, in his forties to fifties when shown in later reign; lean, upright build; olive-brown skin; dark hair and short trimmed beard streaked with grey; lined brow and steady, sorrowful eyes; wears a long undertunic of undyed linen under a deep blue royal cloak edged with woven gold; a simple gold circlet on his brow. Carries no props alone.

payload.title: God arises and scatters enemies
Yahweh is my portion
Jew and the law, true circumcision
Vision of the riders among the myrtle trees

payload.name: Zechariah son of Berechiah
payload.note: The post-exilic prophet Zechariah, son of Berechiah and grandson of Iddo, who prophesies alongside Haggai, receives the visions and oracles of the book bearing his name, and appears in Ezra and Tattenai's letter; one individual across all divisions.

stages.label: Zechariah son of Berechiah

quotes.quote: Yahweh’s word came to the prophet Zechariah the son of Berechiah, the son of Iddo

stages.text: Zechariah son of Berechiah: a man in middle years, lean and weathered, with dark hair and a short full beard touched with grey. Skin olive-brown from desert sun. Deep-set, steady eyes and a calm, grave face. Wears a plain undyed linen tunic under a long cloak of dark brown wool, belted with a cord. Carries a simple wooden staff.

aliases: the angel who talked with me
the man among the myrtle trees
payload.name: The interpreting angel in Zechariah
payload.note: The angel who talks with Zechariah and explains his visions in chapters 1-6; distinct from the angel of Yahweh standing among the myrtle trees.

stages.label: The interpreting angel

quotes.quote: The angel who talked with me said to me, “I will show you what these are.”
The angel who talked with me came again and wakened me, as a man who is wakened out of his sleep.

stages.text: The interpreting angel: a figure of mature, unhurried adult bearing, neither child nor elder; a tall, luminous man with a calm, steady face and dark eyes; skin warm olive-brown; short dark hair and a close-cut beard; wearing a white linen tunic under a long cloak of pale gold, and a priestly sash of blue and crimson; carries no props alone.

aliases: the angel who stood among the myrtle trees
the man on the red horse
payload.name: Yahweh's angel among the myrtle trees
payload.note: The rider among the myrtle trees in chapter 1 who reports on the patrolling horses to Yahweh's angel; distinct from the interpreting angel who talks with Zechariah.

stages.label: Yahweh's angel among the myrtle trees
stages.text: Yahweh's angel among the myrtle trees: a bearded man of mature years, lean and upright, with a steady, grave face, dark eyes and close-cut dark hair and beard touched with light. He wears a long undertunic of white linen under a deep red cloak fastened at the shoulder with a bronze clasp. He rides a red horse. He carries no props.

payload.name: the ravine with the myrtle trees
payload.note: Place where the rider among myrtle trees stands in the first vision.

stages.label: the ravine with the myrtle trees

quotes.quote: he stood among the myrtle trees that were in a ravine

stages.text: the ravine with the myrtle trees: a narrow, shadowed valley floor cut between low limestone hillsides in the Judean highlands. Dense, glossy-leaved myrtle shrubs and small trees grow thickly along the banks, their dark green foliage and white blossoms caught in the dim night air. A dry watercourse winds through the stony ground, with scattered terebinth and rock outcrops. No buildings are visible, only the open, quiet hills rising on either side.

payload.title: Lament over Pharaoh as a monster

payload.name: Ezekiel son of Buzi
payload.note: Exiled priest and prophet at the river Chebar.

stages.label: Ezekiel son of Buzi

quotes.quote: Yahweh’s word came to Ezekiel the priest, the son of Buzi, in the land of the Chaldeans by the river Chebar

stages.text: Ezekiel son of Buzi: a man of about thirty, lean and steady, with dark hair and a short trimmed beard, bronze-brown skin from desert sun, and a calm, watchful face. He wears a plain undyed linen priestly tunic with a long cloak of rough brown wool over it. He carries a wooden writing tablet and stylus.

aliases: the great monster in the river
payload.name: Pharaoh of Ezekiel's oracles (Egyptian king as monster and cedar)
payload.note: The king of Egypt addressed in Ezekiel 29-32 as a river monster and a fallen cedar; a later, separate king in the prophetic oracles, distinguished from the Exodus oppressor by his portrayal and the judgment oracles addressed to him.

stages.label: Pharaoh of Ezekiel's oracles

quotes.quote: the great monster that lies in the middle of his rivers
You were likened to a young lion of the nations; yet you are as a monster in the seas.
You will lie in the middle of the uncircumcised, with those who are slain by the sword.

stages.text: Pharaoh of Ezekiel's oracles: a mature king in his middle years, broad-shouldered and heavy in build, with dark olive skin, long dark hair and a full beard, a stern, weighty face. Wears a pleated linen court robe in deep blue edged with gold, a gold broad collar and a double crown of Egypt. Carries a royal crook and flail as signature props. Strange and fearsome, not comic.

payload.title: Inheritance of Judah

payload.name: Caleb son of Jephunneh
payload.note: Judahite spy who urges entering Canaan, and the man who offers Achsah at Kiriath Sepher in Judges.

stages.label: Caleb

quotes.quote: Of the tribe of Judah, Caleb the son of Jephunneh.
Caleb the son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite said to him

stages.text: Caleb: a strong man in his prime, middle-aged and weathered by desert travel, of medium-to-tall build with broad shoulders. Warm brown skin, short dark hair and a close-cut beard touched with early grey. Calm, steady face with deep-set eyes and a firm mouth. Wears a woven undyed wool tunic under a long cloak of deep earth-red, with a linen head-wrap. Carries a plain wooden staff; no other signature prop.

payload.name: Hebron (city in Judah)
payload.note: The city in Judah given to Caleb, a city of refuge, and the site where David is anointed king and reigns seven years; the same town appears across Joshua, Judges, 2 Samuel and 1 Chronicles.

stages.label: Hebron

quotes.quote: Now the name of Hebron before was Kiriath Arba
Joab took him aside into the middle of the gate
hanged them up beside the pool in Hebron
They buried Abner in Hebron

stages.text: Hebron: a walled hill-country town in Judah on a high ridge, with terraced limestone houses of flat roofs and thick stone walls, a city gate of heavy timber and stone, pastures and vineyards on the slopes, olive and terebinth trees, a deep pool near the gate, and an old tomb cave in the rock.

payload.title: The sword drawn against Jerusalem
Glory returns to the temple and the house is shown

payload.name: Man clothed in linen
payload.note: Heavenly figure who marks the faithful with a mark, scatters coals over the city, and measures the new temple with a reed; treated as one guide throughout Ezekiel.

stages.label: Man clothed in linen

quotes.quote: the man clothed in linen, who had the writer’s inkhorn by his side
Take fire from between the whirling wheels, from between the cherubim

stages.text: Man clothed in linen: a figure of mature, steady presence, neither young nor old; lean and upright build; pale bronze skin with a faint radiance; close-cut dark hair and short beard; calm, grave features. Signature outfit: a long white linen tunic and priestly linen sash, plain and unadorned. Carries a scribe's bronze inkhorn at his side and a measuring reed of cane in hand.

payload.name: Ezekiel's temple
payload.note: The Jerusalem temple of Ezekiel's visions of abominations and the measured new temple.

stages.label: Ezekiel's temple

quotes.quote: so that there was the face of a man toward the palm tree on the one side, and the face of a young lion toward the palm tree on the other side.
There were made on them, on the doors of the nave, cherubim and palm trees, like those made on the walls.
He measured the court, one hundred cubits long and one hundred cubits wide, square. The altar was before the house.

stages.text: Ezekiel's temple: a walled sanctuary on the mountain of Jerusalem, built of pale dressed limestone with cedar panelling, its inner court paved and square, its nave carved with cherubim and palm trees between which a face of a man and a face of a young lion alternate. Gates of the outer court face east, north and south; side chambers rise in three stories. Olive and cedar trees line the courts; a river flows from beneath the threshold.

payload.title: Proverbs on the king, pride and the lot

payload.name: Solomon
payload.note: Son of David and Bathsheba, king of Israel who builds the temple; the same individual across all divisions. Distinguish from the Shulammite's shepherd beloved, who is not Solomon.

stages.label: Solomon, king of Israel

quotes.quote: had Solomon ride on King David’s mule, and brought him to Gihon.
sat down on his throne and caused a throne to be set for the king’s mother

stages.text: Solomon: man in his twenties to forties, lean and upright with a composed, dignified bearing; warm olive-brown skin; dark curly hair and a short, neatly trimmed beard; calm, thoughtful face with a broad brow. Signature outfit: a long deep-blue royal court robe with gold-thread borders over a white linen tunic, and a gold circlet on his head. Signature prop: a plain rod of royal authority carried alone.

payload.name: The king's court
payload.note: The royal court in Proverbs where kings sit on thrones and princes and officials attend; a human court, not the heavenly assembly in Job.

stages.label: The king's court

quotes.quote: Don’t exalt yourself in the presence of the king, or claim a place among great men;

stages.text: The king's court: a broad, stone-paved hall within a royal palace of dressed limestone and cedar beams, its high throne of ivory and gold raised on a few steps at the far end. Walls hung with embroidered linen in deep purple and blue, and tall bronze-capped pillars along the sides. Lamps of olive oil and low, dignified light. Palace gates of stone nearby.

payload.title: The old prophet deceives the man of God

aliases: the prophet who brought him back
payload.name: Old prophet of Bethel
payload.note: Aged prophet living in Bethel who deceives the man of God and buries him.

stages.label: Old prophet of Bethel

quotes.quote: the prophet who brought him back from the way heard of it

stages.text: Old prophet of Bethel: aged, about seventy, lean and bent with years; weathered olive-brown skin; long white hair and a thin white beard; deep-set, sorrowful eyes and lined brow. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic under a dark brown wool cloak. Carries a worn wooden staff.

aliases: the man of God who came from Judah
payload.name: Man of God from Judah
payload.note: Unnamed prophet who denounces Jeroboam's altar at Bethel and dies by a lion; distinct from Elijah and Shemaiah.

stages.label: Man of God from Judah

quotes.quote: He went after the man of God, and found him sitting under an oak.

stages.text: Man of God from Judah: a man in his middle years, lean and weathered from desert travel, with dark skin browned by sun. Short dark hair and a close-trimmed beard streaked with early grey. Steady eyes, lined brow, sober and dignified face. He wears a plain undyed linen tunic, a rough brown wool cloak fastened at the shoulder, and sandals. He carries a plain wooden staff.

payload.name: Bethel (northern golden-calf shrine of Jeroboam)
payload.note: Northern shrine where Jeroboam sets up a golden calf and the man of God denounces the altar in 1 Kings; the setting of the lion and old prophet episode.

stages.label: Bethel, northern shrine

quotes.quote: He set the one in Bethel, and the other he put in Dan.
a man of God came out of Judah by Yahweh’s word to Bethel

stages.text: Bethel: a rocky hill town in the central highlands of Israel, terraced limestone slopes with olive and terebinth trees, low stone houses and a walled sanctuary court on the high ground. At its centre stands a raised stone altar of rough-hewn blocks with horns at its corners, beside a stone high place and a shrine housing a golden calf on a plinth. Cypress and oak border the open ground, and the approach runs up a worn stone road.

payload.title: Commendation of Tychicus and Onesimus; greetings from companions

aliases: the beloved brother and faithful servant
payload.name: Tychicus
payload.note: Paul's faithful companion and beloved brother from Asia, sent as a messenger to Ephesus, Colossae and possibly Crete; all five entries refer to this one individual.

stages.label: Tychicus

quotes.quote: Tychicus and Trophimus of Asia.
Tychicus, the beloved brother and faithful servant in the Lord
fellow bondservant in the Lord.

stages.text: Tychicus: a man of about forty, of middling height and sturdy build from long travel. Olive-brown skin, weathered by roads and sea wind. Short dark hair and a close-cropped beard streaked with early grey. Calm, steady face with deep-set eyes. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic with a dark brown woollen cloak. Carries a leather satchel with a wax-sealed letter case.

aliases: the faithful and beloved brother Onesimus
payload.name: Onesimus
payload.note: Onesimus the Colossian believer sent with Tychicus to Colossae (Colossians 4:9); the same name and Colossian connection, so he is one individual with the runaway slave in Philemon, though the notes here describe him as a fellow believer rather than a slave.

stages.label: Onesimus

quotes.quote: Onesimus, the faithful and beloved brother, who is one of you.
my child Onesimus, whom I have become the father of in my chains,
I am sending him back. Therefore receive him, that is, my own heart,

stages.text: Onesimus: a young man of about twenty-five to thirty; sturdy, lean build; olive-brown skin; short dark curly hair and a closely trimmed beard; calm, earnest face with dark eyes and a steady gaze. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic of ochre-brown under a dark brown wool cloak. Carries a small leather satchel and a wooden walking staff.

payload.name: Aristarchus, fellow prisoner
payload.note: Named in Colossians as Paul's fellow prisoner sending greetings; a companion in captivity, not the traveling companion of Acts by the notes given.

stages.label: Aristarchus, fellow prisoner

quotes.quote: Aristarchus, my fellow prisoner, greets you

stages.text: Aristarchus: a man of about forty to fifty years; medium build, lean and weathered from travel; olive-brown skin; short dark hair and a trimmed beard touched with grey; calm, attentive face with deep-set eyes. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic with a dull ochre-brown woollen cloak. Signature prop: a worn leather satchel strapped across the chest.

payload.name: Mark, cousin of Barnabas
payload.note: Cousin of Barnabas named in Colossians 4:10 with instructions to receive him; identified by his kinship to Barnabas, not by any narrative role.

stages.label: Mark, cousin of Barnabas

quotes.quote: Mark the cousin of Barnabas

stages.text: Mark, cousin of Barnabas: a man of about thirty-five; lean, sturdy build; olive skin weathered by sun and travel; short dark hair and a close-cut beard flecked with grey; a steady, attentive face with deep-set eyes. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic with a dark brown woollen cloak. He carries no props of his own.

payload.name: Justus, fellow worker (Colossians 4:11)
payload.note: A fellow worker of Jewish background named Justus who comforted Paul; a separate individual from the divine Christ, named only in the greetings of Colossians 4.

stages.label: Justus, fellow worker

quotes.quote: These are my only fellow workers for God’s Kingdom who are of the circumcision, men who have been a comfort to me.

stages.text: Justus: a man of about forty, of middle height and sturdy build, with olive-brown skin, short dark hair and a close-trimmed beard streaked with early grey. Lined, steady face with calm, serious eyes. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic with a deep ochre-brown wool cloak. Carries a worn leather scroll case.

aliases: my fellow prisoner in Christ Jesus
payload.name: Epaphras
payload.note: Faithful servant of Christ from Colossae who reports on the Colossians' faith and prays for them, and a fellow prisoner with Paul who sends greetings in Philemon; both entries describe the same individual.

stages.label: Epaphras

quotes.quote: Epaphras our beloved fellow servant, who is a faithful servant of Christ on your behalf
Epaphras, my fellow prisoner in Christ Jesus, greets you

stages.text: Epaphras: a man of middle years, forties, with a lean, weathered build from travel and imprisonment. Olive skin, short dark hair and a close-trimmed beard streaked with grey. Calm, earnest face with deep-set eyes. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic under a dark brown wool cloak. Carries a worn leather satchel of letters.

payload.name: Luke
payload.note: Physician and beloved companion of Paul, who sends greetings in Colossians, is the only companion with Paul in Rome in 2 Timothy, and is named as a fellow worker in Philemon; all three entries describe the same Luke.

stages.label: Luke

quotes.quote: Luke the beloved physician and Demas greet you.
Only Luke is with me.
as do Mark, Aristarchus, Demas, and Luke, my fellow workers.

stages.text: Luke: man in his forties to fifties; sturdy, lean build; olive skin; short greying dark hair and a close-trimmed beard; calm, attentive, intelligent face with deep-set brown eyes and fine lines at the brow. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic with an earth-brown wool cloak. Signature prop: a small leather physician's satchel with a wooden case of medicinal instruments.

payload.name: Demas
payload.note: Companion of Paul who sends greetings in Colossians, later deserts Paul for love of the present world in 2 Timothy, and is mentioned as a fellow worker in Philemon; all three entries describe the same Demas.

stages.label: Demas

quotes.quote: Luke the beloved physician and Demas greet you.
for Demas left me, having loved this present world, and went to Thessalonica
as do Mark, Aristarchus, Demas, and Luke, my fellow workers.

stages.text: Demas: a man of about thirty-five to forty, of middling height and wiry build from travel by sea and road. Olive skin weathered by sun. Dark brown hair cropped above the ears, short beard trimmed close. Level brow, steady dark eyes, a lined but unhurried face. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic of sand-brown with a dark brown wool cloak fastened at one shoulder. Carries a leather satchel of writing scrolls.

payload.name: Paul's prison
payload.note: The Roman imprisonment from which Paul writes these letters; the same place across Philippians, Colossians and Philemon, referred to as his chains or bonds.

stages.label: Paul's prison

quotes.quote: so that it became evident to the whole palace guard, and to all the rest, that my bonds are in Christ,
both in my bonds and in the defense and confirmation of the Good News

stages.text: Paul's prison: a small, low stone chamber within a Roman garrison building, its thick walls of dressed grey limestone, rough-plastered and cool. A single barred window high in one wall admits pale light. Iron rings are set into the stone, with a worn wooden door banded in iron. The floor is packed earth over flagstones, with a straw pallet and a few clay vessels. Beyond the window, glimpses of cypress and a Roman city's roofs.

payload.title: Israel, election and God's mercy
Israel encamps by the sea; Pharaoh pursues; fear

aliases: Pharaoh (king of Egypt who did not know Joseph)
payload.name: Pharaoh of the Exodus (oppressor of Israel)
payload.note: The unnamed king of Egypt in Exodus who enslaves Israel, hardens his heart against Moses and suffers the plagues; the same king recalled in Deuteronomy and cited in Romans 9:17 as the one raised up to show God's power.

stages.label: Pharaoh of the Exodus

quotes.quote: The king of Egypt called for the midwives, and said to them
Pharaoh’s heart was hardened, and he didn’t listen to them

stages.text: Pharaoh of the Exodus: man in his fifties, tall and broad-shouldered, dark brown skin; close-cropped hair under a blue-and-gold nemes headcloth, and a short trimmed false beard of the royal style; calm, hard features with heavy-lidded eyes and a firm mouth. Signature outfit: white linen kilt with a pleated gold-edged apron, broad gold collar, and red-and-gold royal sash. Signature props: gold crook and flail of royal office, carried alone.

payload.name: the Egyptians
payload.note: The Egyptian people, officers and magicians in Exodus who oppress Israel and suffer the plagues; distinguished from the Egyptian magicians of Genesis and from the Chaldeans of Babylon.

stages.label: the Egyptians

quotes.quote: The Egyptians ruthlessly made the children of Israel serve,
They also, the magicians of Egypt, did the same thing with their enchantments.

stages.text: the Egyptians: adults of middle age, broad-shouldered and strong from labour and rank, with warm brown skin and close-cropped black hair, clean-shaven men with short wigs or bare heads, dignified and grave of face. Signature outfit: a pleated white linen kilt or wrap-tunic with a linen cloak in ochre and blue. Signature props: none carried alone; officers may bear a staff of office.

payload.name: Red Sea
payload.note: The sea in Exodus that parts for Israel and closes over Pharaoh's army; distinct from the other seas by its setting in the exodus narrative.

stages.label: Red Sea

quotes.quote: Moses stretched out his hand over the sea, and Yahweh caused the sea to go back by a strong east wind all night
the waters were a wall to them on their right hand and on their left.
You shall encamp opposite it by the sea.

stages.text: Red Sea: a wide, deep arm of open water between desert shores, its surface dark blue-green under wind. Sand dunes and low reddish cliffs line the coast; scattered tamarisk and palms grow at the water's edge. Bare rock outcrops and shallow wadis run down to the shore, and a distant fortified town sits on the northern ridge.

payload.title: Agrippa's response; Paul's words to the court

payload.name: Saul of Tarsus (Paul)
payload.note: Pharisee from Tarsus who persecutes the Way, is converted on the road to Damascus, and becomes the apostle Paul; told apart from the king by his Pharisee and Tarsus background and conversion narrative in Acts.

stages.label: Saul of Tarsus (Paul)

quotes.quote: The witnesses placed their garments at the feet of a young man named Saul.
They led him by the hand and brought him into Damascus.
I am a Pharisee, a son of Pharisees.
But I was born a Roman.

stages.text: Saul/Paul: man in his thirties to fifties, middle height and spare, wiry build worn by travel and hardship. Olive-brown skin, dark hair cropped short, close-trimmed dark beard with grey beginning at the chin. Lined forehead, deep-set dark eyes, strong nose. Signature outfit: plain undyed wool tunic in ochre-brown under a dark brown travelling cloak with a fringed hem. Signature prop: a worn leather writing satchel and a plain wooden walking staff.

payload.name: King Agrippa
payload.note: Herodian king who hears Paul's defense.

stages.label: King Agrippa

quotes.quote: King Agrippa and Bernice arrived at Caesarea and greeted Festus.
Agrippa and Bernice had come with great pomp

stages.text: King Agrippa: a man in his early forties; lean, upright build; olive skin; dark hair cut short and a neatly trimmed dark beard with grey at the chin; composed, watchful face with heavy brows. Signature outfit: a fine white linen tunic under a purple-bordered royal cloak of deep violet, with a gold fibula at the shoulder. Carries a plain ceremonial staff of dark wood with a gold cap.

payload.name: Bernice
payload.note: Sister of King Agrippa who attends the hearing with him.

stages.label: Bernice

quotes.quote: King Agrippa and Bernice arrived at Caesarea and greeted Festus.
Agrippa and Bernice had come with great pomp

stages.text: Bernice: a woman of about forty, dignified and composed; olive-brown skin; dark hair drawn up and bound with gold pins beneath a fine linen veil edged in purple; a tall, straight-backed build; a poised, aristocratic face with dark, steady eyes. Signature outfit: a long layered tunic of deep purple wool under a pale ivory mantle with a gold-thread border. Signature prop: a slim gold diadem at her brow.

payload.name: Porcius Festus
payload.note: Roman governor who succeeds Felix and refers Paul's case to King Agrippa; a different governor from Pilate and from Gedaliah.

stages.label: Porcius Festus

quotes.quote: Festus therefore, having come into the province, after three days went up to Jerusalem from Caesarea.

stages.text: Porcius Festus: a man of about fifty, middle-aged and of sturdy, practical build; olive-brown skin; short dark hair with grey at the temples, closely cropped; a clean-shaven face with a firm jaw and a thoughtful, weathered brow. Signature outfit: a deep purple-edged white toga over a plain ochre tunic, with a bronze fibula at the shoulder. Signature prop: a small wax writing tablet bound in leather.

payload.name: Caesarea Maritima
payload.note: Coastal Roman port city on the Mediterranean, where Cornelius lives, Herod dies, and Paul is held; distinct from Caesarea Philippi in the north.

stages.label: Caesarea Maritima

quotes.quote: Now there was a certain man in Caesarea, Cornelius by name, a centurion of what was called the Italian Regiment,
he went down to Caesarea, and on the next day he sat on the judgment seat

stages.text: Caesarea Maritima: a Roman port city on the Mediterranean coast of Judea, built of pale limestone and mortar. A broad curved harbour with stone moles and wooden-hulled fishing boats, a white-stone city of colonnaded streets, a Roman theatre facing the sea, administrative halls, and bathhouses with arched roofs. Low sea grasses and palms along the shore, dry Mediterranean scrub on the inland rise.

payload.title: Warnings; the Spirit will convict the world

payload.name: The Twelve Disciples (collective)
payload.note: The twelve apostles/disciples as one collective body acting together across the Gospels and Acts; distinct from the individual disciples named within them.

stages.label: The Twelve Disciples (collective)

quotes.quote: Now the names of the twelve apostles are these. The first, Simon, who is called Peter; Andrew, his brother; James the son of Zebedee
One of his disciples, Andrew, Simon Peter’s brother, said to him,

stages.text: The Twelve Disciples: men of about twenty to forty years; sun-browned, lean and sturdy from fishing and walking; olive to weathered brown skin; short or shoulder-length dark hair and close-trimmed beards; plain, earnest faces. Signature outfit: a undyed linen tunic and a rough brown wool cloak with fringed hem. Signature props: a fishing net coiled over one shoulder for Peter and Andrew; a walking staff for travelers.

payload.title: Call to repentance and coming disaster
Warning to Israel and call to leave Babylon

payload.name: Isaiah son of Amoz
payload.note: Prophet who advises Hezekiah; the same prophet across Isaiah, 2 Kings and 2 Chronicles.

stages.label: Isaiah son of Amoz

quotes.quote: The vision of Isaiah the son of Amoz, which he saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem, in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah.
Go, and loosen the sackcloth from off your waist, and take your sandals from off your feet.

stages.text: Isaiah son of Amoz: a man in his fifties, lean and sinewy, with a weathered brown skin of the Judean hill country. Dark hair graying at the temples, worn to the shoulders, and a short, full grey beard. Deep-set, steady eyes and a long, lined face marked by years of hard counsel. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic belted at the waist and a rough brown wool cloak in earth tones. Carries a simple wooden staff, the sign of a traveling prophet.

payload.name: Judah (kingdom and land)
payload.note: The kingdom or land of Judah as a single place across Nehemiah, Isaiah, Joel, Habakkuk and Zephaniah; all entries describe the same territory, distinguished only by the section context in which they appear.

stages.label: Judah

quotes.quote: Woe to those who join house to house, who lay field to field
its gates have been consumed with fire
some of the children of Judah lived in Kiriath Arba and its towns

stages.text: Judah: a hill country of terraced slopes, stony ridges and deep valleys, with walled towns and villages set among olive groves, vineyards and grain fields; Jerusalem on its heights with stone walls, gates and a temple, and fortified citadels; cypress, terebinth and cedar on the uplands.

payload.title: Expulsion of Tobiah and cleansing of the temple rooms

payload.name: Nehemiah son of Hacaliah
payload.note: Cup bearer to Artaxerxes at Susa who rebuilds Jerusalem's wall as governor of Judah and narrates the book; the only Nehemiah described with this work.

stages.label: Nehemiah, governor of Judah

quotes.quote: The words of Nehemiah the son of Hacaliah. Now in the month Chislev, in the twentieth year, as I was in Susa the palace,

stages.text: Nehemiah: a man in his forties, of middling height and spare, dignified build; olive-brown skin; dark hair and a short, neatly trimmed dark beard with some grey at the chin; deep-set, steady eyes and a serious, careworn face. Signature outfit: a long undertunic of undyed linen under a deep indigo wool cloak with a woven band at the hem, plus a plain leather belt. Carries alone a small bronze signet ring on one finger and, on his travels, a plain wooden walking staff.

payload.name: Tobiah the Ammonite
payload.note: Ammonite official opposing Nehemiah in Jerusalem, allied by marriage with Jewish families and given a temple room; distinct from Tobijah the exile who brings gifts in Zechariah.

stages.label: Tobiah the Ammonite

quotes.quote: Sanballat the Horonite and Tobiah the Ammonite servant heard of it, it grieved them exceedingly

stages.text: Tobiah the Ammonite: a man in his middle years, lean and watchful, with a dark-brown beard trimmed close and short dark hair. Olive-brown skin, a sharp nose and deep-set eyes. Signature outfit: a long undertunic of deep blue-violet wool under a court robe of ochre and bronze-brown, with a Persian-style belt. Carries a ring seal of carved stone on a cord.

payload.name: Eliashib
payload.note: High priest in Jerusalem who helps rebuild the sheep gate, later gives Tobiah a room in the temple; grandfather line of Joiada's son.

stages.label: Eliashib, high priest

quotes.quote: Then Eliashib the high priest rose up with his brothers the priests
Eliashib the priest, who was appointed over the rooms of the house of our God

stages.text: Eliashib: a man in his fifties, broad-shouldered and dignified; olive-brown skin; short grey-streaked dark beard and close-cropped hair; lined brow and steady, serious eyes. Signature outfit: white linen priestly tunic and sash with a blue-violet robe over it, and the high priest's linen turban with a gold plate. Carries no props alone.

payload.name: the priests (group)
payload.note: The priestly class of the sons of Aaron who perform the rites of offering in Leviticus and who repair gates, take part in processions and sign the covenant in Nehemiah; both entries are the same priestly body, so they are one cluster.

stages.label: the priests (group)

quotes.quote: Aaron’s sons, the priests, shall present the blood
and some of the priests’ sons with trumpets

stages.text: The priests: adult men, mostly between thirty and fifty, sturdy and unhurried in bearing. Olive to deep bronze skin, short dark or greying beard, close-cropped hair under a linen head covering. Calm, dignified faces. Signature outfit: a white linen tunic and sash, with a plain linen mitre, in cream and off-white. Props: a bronze censer or a trumpet for processional scenes.

aliases: the house which is called by my name
the tent of the daughter of Zion
the house of Yahweh of Armies
payload.name: Yahweh's house in Jerusalem (the temple)
payload.note: The one Jerusalem temple (Yahweh's house, the sanctuary on Mount Moriah) across all references, from Solomon's building through repair, destruction and rebuilding; construction and ruin are later appearance stages, not separate places.

stages.label: Solomon's temple on Mount Moriah

quotes.quote: The house, when it was under construction, was built of stone prepared at the quarry
Within the inner sanctuary was twenty cubits in length, and twenty cubits in width, and twenty cubits in its height.
He overlaid the floor of the house with gold, inside and outside.
Also he made before the house two pillars thirty-five cubits high
He set the sea on the right side of the house eastward and toward the south.

stages.text: Yahweh's house in Jerusalem: a stone temple of finished ashlar on Mount Moriah, roofed with cedar beams, its inner sanctuary panelled in cedar and overlaid with pure gold. Carved cherubim, palm and open flowers cover the doors and walls. Before the house stand two great bronze pillars and a huge bronze molten sea on twelve oxen. Courts of stone surround it, with olive and cypress trees, and the walled city of Jerusalem rises beyond.

payload.title: Samuel's farewell address

payload.name: Samuel
payload.note: Son of Hannah raised at Shiloh, judge and prophet who anoints Saul and David; the child of Eli's temple, not Elkanah.

stages.label: Samuel as a boy at Shiloh

quotes.quote: The child was young.
The child served Yahweh before Eli the priest.
The child Samuel grew on, and increased in favor both with Yahweh and also with men.

stages.text: Samuel: a boy of about ten years, slight and sturdy, with warm brown skin, short dark curly hair and clear, attentive eyes. His signature outfit is a plain undyed linen tunic of pale ochre with a short linen ephod-style sash, bare feet. He carries no props.

stages.label: Samuel as judge and prophet

quotes.quote: Samuel judged the children of Israel in Mizpah.
Fill your horn with oil, and go.
Samuel judged Israel all the days of his life.

stages.text: Samuel: a man in his middle years, lean and upright, with weathered brown skin, a close-trimmed dark beard flecked with grey, short hair and calm, steady eyes. His signature outfit is a long undyed linen tunic belted at the waist under a deep blue wool cloak. He carries a horn of oil at his belt and, on journeys, a plain wooden staff.

payload.name: Elders of Israel in Samuel
payload.note: National Israelite leaders who take the ark to battle and ask Samuel for a king; distinct from the army of Israel.

stages.label: Elders of Israel

quotes.quote: the elders of Israel said
all the elders of Israel gathered themselves together

stages.text: Elders of Israel: a typical member is a mature man of about fifty to sixty; sturdy, unhurried build; warm brown skin; short greying dark hair and a trimmed greying beard; lined, dignified face. Signature outfit: a long undyed linen tunic with a deep indigo wool cloak over the shoulders. Signature prop: a plain wooden staff of office.

payload.name: Gilgal (Saul's coronation and rejection)
payload.note: Site in 1 Samuel where Saul is made king, offers sacrifice and is rebuked by Samuel.

stages.label: Gilgal

quotes.quote: He went from year to year in a circuit to Bethel, Gilgal, and Mizpah
All the people went to Gilgal; and there they made Saul king before Yahweh in Gilgal.

stages.text: Gilgal: a low, open limestone plateau in the Jordan valley near Jericho, with scattered grey standing stones and a rough stone altar of unhewn rock. Terebinth and tamarisk trees at its edges, dry grass, a few mud-brick and fieldstone houses on the rise. Bethel and Mizpah lie on the hills to the west.

payload.title: The city's ruin, the priests' guilt and Edom's doom

payload.name: Zion
payload.note: Personified city of Jerusalem as a mourning widow and captive princess, speaking in the first person in Lamentations 1 and 2; distinct from the collective people of Judah and Jerusalem.

stages.label: Zion, the mourning city-woman

quotes.quote: She has become as a widow, who was great among the nations!
All her gates are desolate. Her priests sigh.
They have clothed themselves with sackcloth. The virgins of Jerusalem hang down their heads to the ground.

stages.text: Zion: a woman of middle years, dignified and grieving, with dark hair bound low and partly veiled, olive skin darkened by ash and dust. Her features are worn and sorrowful. She wears a plain undyed linen robe under a dark sackcloth mantle of brown and grey, with a torn hem. She carries no regalia.

payload.name: Children of Zion (Lamentations)
payload.note: Infants and children who faint in the streets or beg for bread in Lamentations.

stages.label: Children of Zion

quotes.quote: the young children and the infants swoon in the streets of the city
The precious sons of Zion, comparable to fine gold
The tongue of the nursing child clings to the roof of his mouth for thirst.

stages.text: Children of Zion: young boys and girls aged about four to twelve, with slight thin builds worn down by hunger; olive to brown skin dulled with dust; dark hair cropped short or tied back; large dark eyes and sunken cheeks. Plain undyed linen or wool tunics belted with cord, faded to grey-brown, bare feet dusty. Signature prop: a small clay jar or pitcher held close.

payload.name: The priests of Jerusalem
payload.note: Collective body of priests in Lamentations who are killed in the sanctuary; a group, not an individual.

stages.label: Priests of Jerusalem

quotes.quote: Her priests sigh.
Should the priest and the prophet be killed in the sanctuary of the Lord?

stages.text: The priests of Jerusalem: men of middle to later years, lean and dignified, with dark-brown skin, short dark hair and a neatly kept beard flecked with grey. Calm, grave faces marked by sorrow. Signature outfit: a white linen priestly tunic and a linen headband, with a blue-violet cloak over the shoulders. Carry only a bronze censer.

payload.name: Prophets of Jerusalem
payload.note: The prophets of Jerusalem who gave false visions and are blamed for the city's fall, as portrayed in Lamentations.

stages.label: Prophets of Jerusalem

quotes.quote: her prophets find no vision from Yahweh
the sins of her prophets and the iniquities of her priests

stages.text: Prophets of Jerusalem: men in middle age, lean and weathered, with dark skin tanned by sun and a sturdy build. Short dark beards, hair cropped at the neck, deep-set attentive eyes. Signature outfit: a long undyed linen tunic with a dull ochre wool cloak. Each carries a plain wooden staff.

payload.name: The enemies (Jerusalem's foreign adversaries)
payload.note: Collective invaders and persecutors who destroy Jerusalem in Lamentations; a human/national group, not the divine accuser, so keep separate from Satan.

stages.label: The enemies (Jerusalem's foreign adversaries)

quotes.quote: Her adversaries have become the head. Her enemies prosper

stages.text: The enemies: adult men of the Mesopotamian and neighbouring Levantine peoples, aged twenty to fifty, lean and hardened by campaign. Skin weathered tan to olive-brown. Hair short or bound back, beards trimmed close. Stern, watchful faces. Typical dress: a sleeveless or short-sleeved tunic of undyed wool with a leather belt, a bronze-scaled or leather armour, and a dusty brown cloak. Colours: ochre, rust and iron-grey. Carries a spear or curved sword; no other props.

payload.name: The streets of the city
payload.note: Streets and roads where the children faint, the dead lie and the blind wander.

stages.label: The streets of the city

quotes.quote: The roads to Zion mourn, because no one comes to the solemn assembly.
All her gates are desolate.
The stones of the sanctuary are poured out at the head of every street.

stages.text: The streets of the city: narrow, unpaved or rough-stoned lanes winding between low flat-roofed houses of mud brick and dressed limestone, with broken walls and ruined doorways. Dust and ash lie thick; some stones of the sanctuary and fallen gold-toned debris lie at the corners. Sparse dry scrub grows in cracks, and gates stand desolate at the end of roads leading up toward Zion.

aliases: Edom in the land of Uz
payload.name: The wilderness and exile
payload.note: The Lamentations setting of captivity, pursuit and hiding where the exiles dwell or are hunted; a different place from the Egyptian prison despite the shared alias 'the dungeon'.

stages.label: The wilderness and exile

quotes.quote: She dwells among the nations. She finds no rest.
They have cut off my life in the dungeon, and have cast a stone on me.
The breath of our nostrils, the anointed of Yahweh, was taken in their pits

stages.text: The wilderness and exile: arid highland and dry steppe under a pale sky, scattered with stony ravines, cisterns cut into rock, and low flat-roofed mud-brick dwellings and walled settlements of foreign towns. Sparse thorn scrub and dry grass, a few gnarled terebinths, and distant ruined walls of a broken city on the horizon.

payload.title: Remnant returns and approach of invaders
Jehoiada plans the coup

payload.name: Jehoiada, high priest of Judah
payload.note: High priest who hides Joash, crowns him and reforms the temple in Kings; a distinct individual from any other Jehoiada in the index.

stages.label: Jehoiada

quotes.quote: Jehoiada sent and fetched the captains over hundreds
Jehoiada grew old and was full of days, and he died. He was one hundred thirty years old

stages.text: Jehoiada: man of advanced years, lean and upright, with a lined brow and dignified bearing, dark grey-streaked beard and hair kept short beneath a linen head covering. Warm brown skin, deep-set steady eyes. Wears a long white linen priestly tunic with a blue-violet embroidered hem and a breastpiece; carries a plain wooden staff of office.

payload.name: the Carites and the royal guard
