payload.note: Royal guard and captains who protect Joash and seize Athaliah.

stages.label: Carites and royal guard

quotes.quote: The guard stood, every man with his weapons in his hand
The priest delivered to the captains over hundreds the spears and shields that had been King David’s
Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard, a servant of the king of Babylon

stages.text: Carites and royal guard: adult men, roughly twenty-five to forty-five; sturdy, disciplined build; sun-browned Levantine skin; short dark beards and cropped hair, bound at the brow; plain tunics of undyed linen under leather scale-banded cuirasses with a short cloak of deep red wool. Carry a round shield and spear; the captains wear a bronze crested helm.

payload.name: Joash king of Judah
payload.note: Child king of Judah hidden from Athaliah in the temple, crowned at seven, repairs the temple, later turns to idols and kills Zechariah; not the king of Israel.

stages.label: Joash, king of Judah

quotes.quote: Jehoash was seven years old when he began to reign.
His mother’s name was Zibiah of Beersheba.
they hid him from Athaliah, so that he was not slain.

stages.text: Joash: a boy of about seven at his crowning, slight and small-boned, with a young, solemn face, olive-brown skin, and short dark curls. In adulthood he is a lean, grave man of middling height. He wears a plain linen tunic of ochre-cream with a dark blue woven cloak fastened at the shoulder; a narrow gold diadem marks the crown. He carries a small bronze-handled scroll of the covenant.

payload.title: Sin offering of the whole congregation

payload.name: the altar
payload.note: The bronze altar at the door of the Tent of Meeting in Leviticus, where sacrifices are burned; not the Jerusalem temple.

stages.label: the altar

quotes.quote: the altar that is at the door of the Tent of Meeting
the horns of the altar of sweet incense before Yahweh
Fire shall be kept burning on the altar continually; it shall not go out.
He shall kill it on the north side of the altar before Yahweh.

stages.text: the altar: a square hearth of acacia wood overlaid with bronze, set in an open courtyard before the tent door, with projecting horns at its four corners and a fire burning continually upon it; a bronze basin and its base stand near; the ground at its base is worn and ash-grey; a tent of linen hangings rises behind it in the desert.

aliases: the tent of meeting outside the camp
payload.name: the camp of Israel
payload.note: The Israelite encampment in the wilderness, with the tent of meeting set outside it in Exodus 33; the same encampment that Leviticus calls the camp.

stages.label: the camp of Israel

quotes.quote: the pillar of cloud moved from before them, and stood behind them.
quail came up and covered the camp; and in the morning the dew lay around the camp.
Moses used to take the tent and pitch it outside the camp, far away from the camp
outside of the camp to a clean place where the ashes are poured out

stages.text: the camp of Israel: a wide wilderness encampment of dun-coloured tents of woven goat-hair cloth in ordered rows, with a central sanctuary tent and a gate; bare stony desert plain, scattered acacia and tamarisk, distant dark mountain slopes; a pillar of cloud above the camp by day and fire by night; ash-pits and a clean place beyond its edges.

payload.title: Ezra's company and the journey to Jerusalem

payload.name: Ezra the priest and scribe
payload.note: Priest and scribe, son of Seraiah, who leads the return from Babylon and calls for the putting away of foreign wives.

stages.label: Ezra the priest and scribe

quotes.quote: He was a skilled scribe in the law of Moses, which Yahweh, the God of Israel, had given
Now while Ezra prayed and made confession, weeping and casting himself down before God’s house

stages.text: Ezra the priest and scribe: a man in his middle years, lean and upright, with dark-grey-streaked brown hair and a short trimmed beard. Olive-brown skin, deep-set serious eyes, lined brow. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen priestly tunic and white linen mitre-cap with a dark-blue woven sash, over which a long undyed wool cloak. Carries a rolled scroll of the law in a leather case.

payload.name: People of Judah and Benjamin (Ezra)
payload.note: The returned exiles gathered in Jerusalem who act together in the assembly in Ezra.

stages.label: People of Judah and Benjamin

quotes.quote: and all Israel in their cities.
The children of Israel, the priests, the Levites, and the rest of the children of the captivity

stages.text: People of Judah and Benjamin: a typical member is an adult Israelite man or woman of working age, between about 25 and 55, of sturdy, weathered build from farm and building labour. Skin olive-brown, hair dark and often covered by a head cloth; men bearded, short beards kept trimmed. Faces lined, serious and dignified. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic with a long brown or indigo wool cloak; sandals. Props carried alone: a simple clay water jar or a builder's tool.

aliases: the river that runs to Ahava
payload.name: River Ahava
payload.note: The waterway near Ahava where Ezra gathers the returning exiles and fasts before the journey to Jerusalem; a river in Babylonia-to-Judah travel context, not the Chebar.

stages.label: River Ahava

quotes.quote: I gathered them together to the river that runs to Ahava
Then we departed from the river Ahava on the twelfth day of the first month

stages.text: River Ahava: a slow, broad canal-river of the Babylonian plain, its brown water running between low earthen banks lined with reeds, tamarisk and date palms. Mudbrick embankments and irrigation cuts mark the flat, fertile land; beyond the banks stretch open fields and distant palm groves under a wide, pale sky.

payload.title: Appointment of the seven

payload.name: the seven chosen to serve tables
payload.note: The seven men chosen to serve the widows, including Stephen and Philip.

stages.label: the seven chosen to serve tables

quotes.quote: Philip the evangelist, who was one of the seven

stages.text: the seven chosen to serve tables: men of mature age, late twenties to fifties; sturdy, unhurried build; olive to brown skin; short dark hair and close-trimmed beards, some greying; calm, attentive faces. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic with a brown wool cloak. Props: none alone.

payload.name: The disciples
payload.note: The early Jerusalem assembly of believers acting together in Acts, who choose Matthias and receive the Spirit at Pentecost.

stages.label: The disciples

quotes.quote: Peter stood up in the middle of the disciples (and the number of names was about one hundred twenty)

stages.text: The disciples: a typical member is an adult of about thirty to fifty years, of Jewish Galilean or Judean stock, with olive-brown skin, short dark hair and a close-cut beard, lean and sun-weathered from fishing and travel. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic of ochre-brown with a dark blue wool cloak. Carries no props alone.

payload.name: Hellenist widows
payload.note: The widows of the Hellenist Jews neglected in the daily food serving in Jerusalem (Acts 6), the cause of the complaint; distinct from the widows of Joppa who mourn Tabitha.

stages.label: Hellenist widows

quotes.quote: All the widows stood by him weeping, and showing the tunics and other garments which Dorcas had made

stages.text: Hellenist widows: women from middle age to elderly, slender to sturdy build, olive to light brown skin, dark hair covered by a linen veil or head cloth, lined faces of quiet dignity. Signature outfit: a long undyed linen tunic with a dark wool mantle in deep blue or brown, plain and well kept. No props carried alone.

payload.title: Old age and continued trust
Prayer for the rending of the heavens
Praise for Yahweh's acts in history
Witnesses to the Son

aliases: the chief priests and elders of the council
payload.name: The Jewish leaders
payload.note: The Johannine Jewish authorities and opponents of Jesus, including Pharisees, priests and scribes acting as one opposing body in John's disputes.

stages.label: The Jewish leaders

quotes.quote: when the Jews sent priests and Levites from Jerusalem to ask him
there was a man of the Pharisees named Nicodemus, a ruler of the Jews
Your own nation and the chief priests delivered you to me.

stages.text: The Jewish leaders: men of middle to later years, roughly thirty to sixty; lean to sturdy build; olive to bronze skin; closely trimmed dark beards, grey at the edges; dignified, careful faces. Signature outfit: a long linen tunic with a fringed prayer shawl (tallit) in white and blue, with phylacteries on the forehead and arm. Signature prop: a scroll of the law held in the hands.

payload.title: The people bring their gifts
Escape from Sodom

payload.name: Lot
payload.note: Abram's nephew, son of Haran, who settles in Sodom and escapes its destruction with his daughters; the same Lot described in 2 Peter as the righteous man delivered from the cities of the plain, so both entries are one individual.

stages.label: Lot

quotes.quote: Haran became the father of Lot.
Lot his brother’s son, all their possessions that they had gathered
Lot also, who went with Abram, had flocks, herds, and tents.
Lot sat in the gate of Sodom.

stages.text: Lot: a man in his middle years, sturdy and weathered from herding, with a lean wiry build, olive-brown skin, short dark hair and a close-trimmed beard streaked with grey at the chin, deep-set brown eyes and lined brow. Signature outfit: a long undyed wool tunic in ochre with a dark brown wool wrap over the shoulders and leather sandals. Signature prop: a shepherd's crook of dark wood.

payload.name: The three visitors at Mamre and the two angels at Sodom
payload.note: The three men who visit Abraham and the two angels who rescue Lot in Genesis, treated as one group of visitors; not the two white-robed angels at the empty tomb in John.

stages.label: The visitors (typical member)

quotes.quote: The two angels came to Sodom at evening. Lot sat in the gate of Sodom.

stages.text: The visitors: men of mature adult age, neither young nor old; lean and sturdy build; skin weathered brown by desert sun; short dark beard and hair cropped close to the head; calm, grave face with deep-set eyes. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen wrap over a short wool tunic in earth brown, with leather sandals. Carries a plain wooden staff, the only prop.

payload.name: Lot's wife
payload.note: Wife of Lot who looks back at Sodom and becomes a pillar of salt.

stages.label: Lot's wife
stages.text: Lot's wife: a woman of middle age, sturdy and weathered from desert life; olive-brown skin; dark hair bound under a plain linen head-cloth; lined, careful face. Her signature outfit is a long undyed wool wrap over a simple linen tunic in earthy ochre and dun, with leather sandals. She carries no props.

payload.name: Lot's daughters
payload.note: Two daughters of Lot who make him drink wine and conceive by him; act together in the cave.

stages.label: Lot's daughters
stages.text: Lot's daughters: young women of about fifteen to twenty; slender, sturdy build; olive skin; dark hair worn long, braided and covered by a linen headcloth; calm, grave features. Signature outfit: long undyed wool tunic under a dusky-red woven wrap, with plain leather sandals. No signature props.

aliases: the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah
payload.name: Sodom
payload.note: The wicked city of the plain destroyed by fire and sulfur in Genesis, appearing as the cities of the plain and in 2 Peter as Sodom and Gomorrah together; both entries refer to this one place.

stages.label: Sodom

quotes.quote: all the plain of the Jordan, that it was well-watered everywhere
Lot sat in the gate of Sodom.
the valley of Siddim was full of tar pits

stages.text: Sodom: a walled city of sun-dried mud-brick on the well-watered plain of the Jordan, its gate the centre of civic life; flat-roofed houses stacked close, date palms and irrigated gardens beyond the walls, and low hills to the east; the Valley of Siddim nearby, its ground dark with tar pits.

payload.name: Zoar
payload.note: Small city where Lot takes refuge before the destruction of Sodom.

stages.label: Zoar

quotes.quote: it was well-watered everywhere, before Yahweh destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah, like the garden of Yahweh
he was afraid to live in Zoar. He lived in a cave

stages.text: Zoar: a small mud-brick town on the well-watered plain of the Jordan, its low walls and flat roofs of sun-dried brick rising beside irrigated fields, palms and tamarisk, and wells at its edge. Beyond the town the land runs toward dry hills and a rising mountain country with caves in its rock.

payload.title: Servants and the example of Christ

payload.name: The chosen ones of the Dispersion
payload.note: Scattered believers across Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia and Bithynia addressed as elect foreigners; told apart by their dispersion and the living-stones imagery.

stages.label: The chosen ones of the Dispersion

quotes.quote: the chosen ones who are living as foreigners in the Dispersion in Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia
You also as living stones are built up as a spiritual house
I beg you as foreigners and pilgrims

stages.text: The chosen ones of the Dispersion: a typical believer, a man or woman in middle age, roughly 30 to 50; sturdy, weathered build from labour and travel; olive to tawny skin; dark hair kept short or covered by a simple cloth, beards trimmed; calm, steady face. Plain undyed linen tunic in ochre or sand, over it a dark brown wool cloak worn against the weather; leather sandals. Carries a wooden staff as a pilgrim.

payload.title: Yahweh the keeper of Israel
Jacob meets Rachel at the well

payload.name: Jacob
payload.note: Younger twin son of Isaac and Rebekah, renamed Israel after wrestling with God and father of the twelve sons; the central patriarch of Genesis, also referenced by name in Hosea, Obadiah, Malachi and the New Testament letters.

stages.label: Jacob

quotes.quote: The voice is Jacob’s voice, but the hands are the hands of Esau.
Isn’t he rightly named Jacob?
his hand had hold on Esau’s heel
leaning on the top of his staff.

stages.text: Jacob: a slender, wiry man of middle to later years in his prime and sixties-to-seventies in old age; lean, sinewy build from long herding; smooth, unhairy skin browned by sun; dark, close-cropped hair and short beard kept trim; alert, thoughtful eyes and a clean, quiet face. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic and wool wrap cloak in earth brown, with leather sandals. Carries a shepherd's staff.

payload.name: Rachel
payload.note: Younger daughter of Laban, beloved wife of Jacob, mother of Joseph and Benjamin; dies in childbirth.

stages.label: Rachel

quotes.quote: Rachel was beautiful in form and attractive.
Rachel came with her father’s sheep, for she kept them.

stages.text: Rachel: a young woman of about eighteen to twenty-five, slender and graceful, of good height; warm olive-brown skin, dark almond eyes, full dark brown hair worn long and bound with a linen band; fine, attractive features. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic belted at the waist with a deep indigo wool wrap over the shoulders, simple leather sandals. Signature prop: a wooden shepherd's staff.

payload.name: Laban
payload.note: Brother of Rebekah in Haran; hosts Jacob, gives him Leah and Rachel, and makes a covenant with him at Gilead.

stages.label: Laban of Haran

quotes.quote: Rebekah had a brother, and his name was Laban. Laban ran out to the man, to the spring.
When Laban heard the news of Jacob, his sister’s son, he ran to meet Jacob, and embraced him, and kissed him, and brought him to his house.

stages.text: Laban: a man in his middle years, past youth but vigorous, with a sturdy build from herding and travel. Skin weathered olive-brown. Dark hair cropped close at the neck, a short full beard greying at the chin. Calm, watchful eyes and a broad, lined face. Signature outfit: a long undergarment of undyed wool beneath a rust-red wool mantle, leather sandals, a leather belt at the waist. Carries a herdsman's staff of dark wood.

payload.name: Haran
payload.note: City where Terah dies and where Laban lives; Jacob's refuge and home of Rebekah's family.

stages.label: Haran

quotes.quote: They came to Haran and lived there.
We are from Haran.

stages.text: Haran: a settled town on the open plains of Northern Mesopotamia, flat grassland and dry steppe under wide skies, with wells at its edge and irrigated fields of barley. Low mud-brick houses with flat roofs cluster around a walled enclosure and a sheepfold, with a shrine or altar on a raised platform. Date palms, tamarisk and pistachio trees line the water channels; flocks graze the outer pastures.

payload.title: Run the race looking to Jesus
Submission to authority and love
Plague of frogs and Pharaoh's respite
Conquest of the southern cities

payload.name: Joshua son of Nun
payload.note: Son of Nun of Ephraim, Moses' aide and successor who leads Israel into Canaan; the same individual across Exodus, Numbers, Deuteronomy, Joshua, Judges (as the deceased) and Hebrews, so no other Joshua is separated from him in this group.

stages.label: Joshua son of Nun

quotes.quote: Joshua defeated Amalek and his people with the edge of the sword.
his servant Joshua, the son of Nun, a young man, didn’t depart from the Tent.
Joshua was old and well advanced in years

stages.text: Joshua son of Nun: a man of mature strength in his prime, aged about forty to fifty when leading, with a sturdy, broad-shouldered build and weathered brown skin marked by desert sun. Short dark hair, close-cropped beard, steady deep-set eyes and a firm, grave face. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic and a dark brown woven wool cloak. Carries a bronze-bladed sword at his belt and a long wooden spear.

payload.name: Makkedah
payload.note: City with a cave where the five kings hide.

stages.label: Makkedah

quotes.quote: These five kings fled, and hid themselves in the cave at Makkedah.
Joshua took Makkedah on that day, and struck it with the edge of the sword, with its king.

stages.text: Makkedah: a fortified walled town on a low rise of the southern Shephelah, with rough stone and mud-brick houses and a gate tower of dressed limestone. Terraced fields of barley and olive trees lie below the walls, and dry scrub grows on the rocky slopes. A cave opens in the limestone escarpment just beyond the town, its mouth wide enough for men to enter.

payload.name: Gilgal (Joshua's camp near Jericho)
payload.note: Israelite camp near Jericho in Joshua where memorial stones are set up and circumcision occurs; the camp at Gilgal named in Joshua.

stages.label: Gilgal, the camp near Jericho

quotes.quote: encamped in Gilgal, on the east border of Jericho
Joshua set up those twelve stones, which they took out of the Jordan, in Gilgal.
They kept the Passover on the fourteenth day of the month at evening in the plains of Jericho.

stages.text: Gilgal: a broad level plain on the east border of Jericho, the Jordan valley lowland with dry clay and scrubby grass. Ranks of goat-hair and linen tents, with a central open space; twelve rough-hewn stones of river rock set in a rough circle as a memorial. Sparse tamarisk and palm near the riverbank; the walled city of Jericho visible to the west on a low rise.

payload.title: Elijah and Elisha go toward the Jordan

aliases: the man of God on the hill
payload.name: Elijah
payload.note: Tishbite prophet of Gilead who confronts Ahab, calls fire on Carmel and is taken up by a whirlwind; the same prophet in 1 Kings and 2 Kings, rebuking Ahaziah and parting the Jordan.

stages.label: Elijah

quotes.quote: He was a hairy man, and wearing a leather belt around his waist.
Elijah the Tishbite, who was one of the settlers of Gilead
Elijah took his mantle, and rolled it up, and struck the waters

stages.text: Elijah: a lean, weathered man of middle years; sinewy build, tall and spare; sun-darkened skin; long, unkempt hair and a full wild beard; deep-set, unflinching eyes. Signature outfit in dark brown sheepskin mantle over a rough undertunic, girded with a plain leather belt; colours of earth, umber and ash. Carries only his mantle, which he rolls and strikes with.

payload.name: Elisha son of Shaphat
payload.note: Prophet, Elijah's successor, who first appears as a farmer plowing with twelve yoke of oxen in 1 Kings and is later named in 2 Kings and Luke; the same prophet in all three entries.

stages.label: Elisha son of Shaphat

quotes.quote: found Elisha the son of Shaphat, who was plowing with twelve yoke of oxen before him
Elijah went over to him and put his mantle on him.
He took Elijah’s mantle that fell from him
He went up from there to Bethel. As he was going up by the way, some youths came out of the city and mocked him, and said to him, “Go up, you baldy! Go up, you baldy!”

stages.text: Elisha son of Shaphat: a man in his middle years, broad-shouldered and sun-browned from working the fields, lean and steady in build. Dark skin, a bald head, and a close-cut beard with some grey at the chin. Calm, weathered face with deep-set eyes. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic belted at the waist with a cloak of rough brown wool. Signature prop: Elijah's mantle, a dark sheepskin cloak he wears over his shoulders.

payload.name: the Jordan River
payload.note: The single river Jordan across all five books: crossed dryshod by Israel near Jericho in Joshua, crossed by Elijah and Elisha in 2 Kings, and the baptism site of John and Jesus in the Gospels; all entries refer to this same river.

stages.label: The Jordan River

quotes.quote: the Jordan overflows all its banks all the time of harvest
The east border was the Salt Sea, even to the end of the Jordan.

stages.text: The Jordan River: a broad, swift river running south through a deep rift valley from the hills of Galilee to the Salt Sea. Its banks are steep, lined with tamarisk, willow and reeds, with wide flood-plains and thickets that fill when it overflows at harvest. Fords cross its shallows near Jericho, and palm-shaded terraces rise to the hill country on either side. Stone and mudbrick towns stand above the banks.

payload.name: Bethel (prophets' community and calf shrine in Kings)
payload.note: Town in 2 Kings with a prophets' community and golden-calf shrine, where Elisha is mocked by youths and Josiah acts against the shrine; the same northern shrine tradition as in 1 Kings.

stages.label: Bethel, hill town with calf shrine

quotes.quote: So they went down to Bethel.
some youths came out of the city
the golden calves that were in Bethel and that were in Dan
the altar that was at Bethel and the high place

stages.text: Bethel: a walled hill town on a rocky ridge of central Judah-Israel highland, terraced olive groves and terebinths on the slopes, low flat-roofed stone and mud-brick houses, a city gate of heavy timber and stone, and a raised high place with an altar of dressed stone and an Asherah pole beside it, with the golden-calf shrine as its central landmark.

payload.name: Jericho
payload.note: The one walled city of Jericho in the Bible; all six entries describe this same place in Joshua, 2 Kings, the Gospels and Hebrews, so they are one cluster.

stages.label: Jericho, the city of palms

quotes.quote: Now Jericho was tightly shut up because of the children of Israel. No one went out, and no one came in.
going up from Jericho through the hill country to Bethel.
By faith the walls of Jericho fell down after they had been encircled for seven days.
With the loss of his firstborn he will lay its foundation, and with the loss of his youngest son he will set up its gates.

stages.text: Jericho: a walled city on the plains beside the Jordan, near the Dead Sea, with broad flat terrain of sun-bleached earth and sparse scrub. Tall date palms rise among the houses and gardens, and mud-brick and stone walls ring the city, with a heavy timber-and-stone gate. Limestone hills climb westward behind it toward the hill country, with a rough road cut into the slope.

payload.title: Return of backsliding Israel
Josiah's death at Megiddo

payload.name: Josiah
payload.note: Reforming king of Judah who finds the book of the law; also named as the reigning king in Zephaniah.

stages.label: Josiah, king of Judah

quotes.quote: Josiah was eight years old when he began to reign, and he reigned thirty-one years in Jerusalem.
In the eighteenth year of King Josiah, the king sent Shaphan, the son of Azaliah the son of Meshullam, the scribe, to Yahweh’s house

stages.text: Josiah: a man in his late twenties to thirties at his reforms, lean and upright, of medium height. Olive-brown skin, close-cropped dark hair and a short trimmed beard. Calm, grave, steady face with deep-set eyes. Signature outfit: a long undertunic of undyed linen under a deep blue court robe with a gold-edged hem, and a plain royal circlet of gold. Carries a plain wooden scribe's writing case at the belt.

payload.name: Pharaoh Necoh
payload.note: Egyptian king who kills Josiah at Megiddo, deposes Jehoahaz and is struck at Carchemish; distinct from the earlier Pharaohs.

stages.label: Pharaoh Necoh

quotes.quote: Pharaoh Necoh king of Egypt went up against the king of Assyria to the river Euphrates

stages.text: Pharaoh Necoh: man in his middle years, lean and upright, dark brown skin, close-cropped hair under a tall royal nemes headcloth striped gold and blue, clean-shaven with a short ceremonial false beard, calm hard features, dark kohl-lined eyes. Signature outfit: a pleated white linen kilt with a gold belt and a broad collar of gold and lapis, in royal blue and gold. Carries a gold-tipped crook and flail as royal insignia.

payload.name: Megiddo
payload.note: The city and valley of Megiddo, site of King Josiah's fatal battle with Necoh; the 2-Kings and 2-Chronicles entries describe the same place, so they are joined.

stages.label: Megiddo

quotes.quote: Pharaoh Necoh killed him at Megiddo
came to fight in the valley of Megiddo

stages.text: Megiddo: a broad fertile valley of barley fields and olive groves below a tall mound city of mudbrick walls on dressed stone footings. Cut-stone city gate with a pair of projecting towers; a grain silo and water shaft; low hills rising north and south; a few sycamores and terebinths along the valley road.

payload.title: Oracles against the kings
Wisdom's creative role and everyday counsel
Settling Jerusalem and listing its residents

payload.name: The nobles and rulers of Judah
payload.note: Leading men of Judah in Nehemiah rebuked for usury and Sabbath trading; a civil elite of post-exilic Judah, not the temple priesthood.

stages.label: The nobles and rulers of Judah

quotes.quote: I consulted with myself, and contended with the nobles and the rulers

stages.text: The nobles and rulers of Judah: a typical member is a man of middle age, lean and dignified, with a sturdy build, olive-brown skin, and a short dark beard trimmed close. His hair is dark and kept to the shoulder, bound with a plain cord. His face is grave and careful. He wears a long undertunic of undyed linen under a blue-violet court robe with a woven band at the hem, and a leather belt. Signature prop: a seal ring of dark stone on his finger.

aliases: Jeshua, Bani, Sherebiah and the Levites
payload.name: The Levites who teach the law (Nehemiah)
payload.note: Levites in Nehemiah who explain the law, lead prayer and confession, and appear in the register of priests and Levites; they are a teaching and prayer group rather than the tabernacle service crew.

stages.label: The Levites who teach the law

quotes.quote: Also Jeshua, Bani, Sherebiah, Jamin, Akkub, Shabbethai, Hodiah, Maaseiah, Kelita, Azariah, Jozabad, Hanan, Pelaiah, and the Levites, caused the people to understand the law
Then Jeshua, Bani, Kadmiel, Shebaniah, Bunni, Sherebiah, Bani, and Chenani of the Levites stood up on the stairs, and cried with a loud voice to Yahweh their God.

stages.text: The Levites who teach the law: men of middle age, lean and sure-footed, with brown skin weathered by the Judean sun. Dark hair worn to the shoulder, beards trimmed short and neat. Plain undyed linen tunic belted at the waist, over it a long wool cloak in undyed brown or ochre. Carry a wooden staff or a scroll case of leather.

payload.name: Ophel
payload.note: Hill district near the temple where the temple servants live.

stages.label: Ophel, the temple servants' hill district

quotes.quote: the temple servants lived in Ophel, to the place opposite the water gate toward the east, and the tower that stands out
opposite the great tower that stands out, and to the wall of Ophel
But the temple servants lived in Ophel

stages.text: Ophel: a spur of rising ground inside the walls of Jerusalem, sloping down toward the east near the water gate, its terraces of pale limestone. Low flat-roofed houses of dressed stone and mud brick line narrow lanes. Olive trees, fig and vine grow in small courtyards; dry grass on the slopes. A tall outstanding tower and a stretch of new wall rise nearby against the sky.

payload.title: Vision of the new temple's gates
Laws on theft, damage, and seduction
Release and final defeat of Satan

aliases: the nations at the four corners of the earth
payload.name: Gog and Magog
payload.note: The collective nations gathered by Satan after the thousand years to surround the camp of the saints (Revelation 20); a multitude of peoples, not one prince.

stages.label: The gathered nations

quotes.quote: the nations which are in the four corners of the earth, Gog and Magog
whose number is as the sand of the sea

stages.text: Gog and Magog: a typical member of the gathered nations is an adult of middle years, sturdy and weathered, of varied skin tones, with dark hair bound back and short, close beards. Faces are grave and resolute. Each wears a practical wrapped tunic of undyed linen and wool in earth browns, ochres and deep red, with leather bracing, and carries a plain staff or a short spear of ash wood.

aliases: the prince of the power of the air
the spirit who works in the children of disobedience
the deceiver of the whole world
payload.name: Satan
payload.note: The one adversary figure (Satan, the devil, the tempter, the evil one, the dragon) across all supplied entries; distinguished from other figures only by being the accuser and tempter of humankind.

stages.label: Satan, the adversary and great red dragon

quotes.quote: The great dragon was thrown down, the old serpent, he who is called the devil and Satan
From going back and forth on the earth, and from walking up and down in it.

stages.text: Satan: no human face or body; a vast, fearsome serpentine shape of deep red and dark scale, coiled and many-headed in the manner of the great red dragon, with a shadowed, unlit core. Visionary and strange, not comic.

payload.name: The earth
payload.note: The inhabited world where the plagues and the beasts of Revelation fall.

stages.label: The earth

quotes.quote: hid themselves in the caves and in the rocks of the mountains
something like a sea of glass mixed with fire
all green grass was burned up
gather the clusters of the vine of the earth

stages.text: The earth: a wide inhabited world of land and sea, with mountains, rock-faced caves, green grass, fig and olive trees, and vine-covered hills, under a great sky; the sea is calm and clear as glass mixed with fire, and the coasts hold sand, harbours and cities of stone.

payload.title: Wisdom on the fate of the wicked and righteous
Warnings against empty argument and false teachers

payload.name: Paul's prison in Rome
payload.note: Paul's Roman imprisonment where he writes 2 Timothy while awaiting execution; the Rome setting distinguishes it from the Philemon letter's prison.

stages.label: Paul's prison in Rome

quotes.quote: but when he was in Rome, he sought me diligently and found me

stages.text: Paul's prison in Rome: a low, windowless chamber of rough-hewn grey stone set into the foundation of a Roman city structure, with heavy iron-banded wooden door and a narrow barred grating high in the wall. Bare stone floor, scant straw, a few rough wooden fixtures. Little vegetation; faint moss in damp corners; the stonework of imperial Rome beyond.

payload.title: Announcement of betrayal at supper

aliases: the thief with the money box
payload.name: Judas Iscariot
payload.note: The apostle who betrays Jesus for money, appearing in all five Gospel and Acts entries; the same individual in every division, distinct from Judas the brother of James.

stages.label: Judas Iscariot

quotes.quote: one of the twelve, who was called Judas Iscariot, went to the chief priests
because Judas had the money box

stages.text: Judas Iscariot: a man of about thirty-five, of medium height and wiry build, with olive-brown skin, close-cropped dark hair and a short trimmed beard. Angular face, deep-set brown eyes, a watchful and careful look. Plain undyed linen tunic in earth brown under a dark ochre wool cloak. Carries a leather money box on a cord at his belt.

payload.title: Commissioning of Joshua, the Song, and the sentence on Moses

aliases: the priests who bear the ark
payload.name: The priests and Levites (Deuteronomy)
payload.note: The Levitical priests who bear the ark and minister and judge in Deuteronomy's ritual and legal scenes.

stages.label: The priests and Levites

quotes.quote: the priests the sons of Levi, who bore the ark of Yahweh’s covenant
You shall command the priests who bear the ark of the covenant

stages.text: The priests and Levites: adult men of middle age, sturdy and dignified; olive-brown skin of the Levant; close-cropped dark hair and a short trimmed beard; calm, grave features. Signature outfit: a white woven linen tunic and sash with a blue-violet priestly robe and cloak, plain and clean. Carry the ark's poles on the shoulder.

payload.name: Elders, judges and officers of Deuteronomy
payload.note: Tribal judges and officers who hear cases and receive the law in Deuteronomy.

stages.label: Elders, judges and officers of Deuteronomy

quotes.quote: then both the men, between whom the controversy is, shall stand before Yahweh, before the priests and the judges
then his father and his mother shall take hold of him and bring him out to the elders of his city and to the gate of his place.

stages.text: Elders, judges and officers: men of middle to advanced age, mostly weathered and grey-bearded; sturdy build; olive-brown skin; short grey-streaked beards and close-cropped hair; calm, serious faces. Signature outfit: a long woven undertunic of undyed linen under a deep indigo cloak with a plain woven border. Carry a short wooden staff of office.

payload.name: The plains of Moab
payload.note: Eastern camp across the Jordan where Moses speaks the law and dies, Deuteronomy only.

stages.label: The plains of Moab

quotes.quote: Beyond the Jordan, in the land of Moab, Moses began to declare this law
Moses went up from the plains of Moab to Mount Nebo, to the top of Pisgah, that is opposite Jericho.
in the valley opposite Beth Peor, in the land of Sihon king of the Amorites

stages.text: The plains of Moab: a broad, low valley of dry grassland and scrub east of the Jordan, opposite Jericho and Beth Peor, with acacia, tamarisk and wild shrubs along the river line. Rising to the west, the bare slopes of Mount Nebo and Pisgah, with a flat-topped summit, look over the Jordan valley. Plain tents of goat hair and rough stone walls mark the Israelite encampment; no buildings of note stand in the valley.

payload.name: Mount Nebo and Pisgah
payload.note: Mountain heights east of the Jordan in Numbers where Balaam views Israel and Moses views the land; distinct from the Israelite mountains and Edom.

stages.label: Mount Nebo and Pisgah

quotes.quote: He took him into the field of Zophim, to the top of Pisgah, and built seven altars
under the slopes of Pisgah eastward.
Moses went up from the plains of Moab to Mount Nebo, to the top of Pisgah, that is opposite Jericho.

stages.text: Mount Nebo and Pisgah: a bare, rounded ridge of pale limestone rising east of the Jordan in the highlands of Moab, its upper slopes broken by grey outcrops and scattered scrub. Below its flanks the Arabah stretches toward the Salt Sea. On the summit stand low, rough-hewn stone altars and a few dry terraces, with no town or dwelling in view.

payload.title: Yahweh on the wild animals

payload.name: Job
payload.note: Blameless, wealthy man of Uz who loses his family and health and debates with his friends and with Yahweh.

stages.label: Job

quotes.quote: There was a man in the land of Uz, whose name was Job. That man was blameless and upright, and one who feared God, and turned away from evil.
Then Job arose, and tore his robe, and shaved his head, and fell down on the ground, and worshiped.
So Satan went out from the presence of Yahweh, and struck Job with painful sores from the sole of his foot to his head.

stages.text: Job: man of middle to later years, perhaps fifty to sixty, of sturdy but weathered build; dark brown skin; short, graying hair with a close-trimmed beard shaved at the head in grief; dignified, lined face with deep-set eyes. Signature outfit: a long undyed linen tunic with a deep indigo wool cloak over it. Carries a shepherd's staff of olive wood. Sores on skin in later sections.

payload.name: The whirlwind
payload.note: Place from which Yahweh speaks to Job (38:1, 40:6).

stages.label: The whirlwind

quotes.quote: Then Yahweh answered Job out of the whirlwind,
Then Yahweh answered Job out of the whirlwind:

stages.text: The whirlwind: a great column of storm wind rising from a dark wilderness sky, funnelling dust, torn cloud and scattered grit in dense swirling bands. Heavy grey-brown cloud churns above, its edges lit faintly from behind. Low scrub and bare desert ground are flattened and whipped by the gale.

payload.title: Ordeal of jealousy
Daniel describes the dream of the great image

payload.name: Daniel (prophet of Babylon)
payload.note: The Jewish youth taken captive to Babylon, renamed Belteshazzar, who interprets dreams and receives visions; the main entry with many sections in Daniel, distinguished from the prophet named only in Matthew's citation.

stages.label: Daniel (Belteshazzar), prophet of Babylon

quotes.quote: Now among these of the children of Judah were Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah.
to Daniel he gave the name Belteshazzar
he went into his house (now his windows were open in his room toward Jerusalem)

stages.text: Daniel: a lean, dignified Judean man in his youth grown to a grave, graying elder; olive-brown skin; dark hair cropped close and a short trimmed beard flecked with grey; deep-set, steady eyes and a calm, thoughtful face. Signature outfit: a long undyed linen tunic under a plain indigo wool cloak with a blue fringed hem. Props: a small leather scroll case slung at the hip.

payload.name: Royal palace of Babylon
payload.note: Babylonian palace where the king receives counsel, sees the handwriting and hears Daniel's interpretations; distinct from the Susa palace.

stages.label: Royal palace of Babylon

quotes.quote: he was walking in the royal palace of Babylon

stages.text: Royal palace of Babylon: a vast walled complex on the flat alluvial plain of the Euphrates, built of sun-dried and fired brick glazed in deep blue with yellow lion and dragon reliefs. Tiered terraces rise toward a great gate with tall towers; hanging gardens of palms, date trees and climbing vines spill over the walls. Broad courts of pale stone lead to a banquet hall with high cedar-beamed ceilings and a river-facing colonnade.

payload.title: The wilderness rebellion and the unbelieving generation

payload.name: The wilderness (Hebrews testing)
payload.note: The place of Israel's testing and forty years of rebellion as recalled in Hebrews.

stages.label: The wilderness

quotes.quote: in the day of the trial in the wilderness
whose bodies fell in the wilderness
wandering in deserts, mountains, caves, and the holes of the earth

stages.text: The wilderness: a vast arid desert of pale sand and broken limestone, rising into bare mountains and ridges cut by dry wadis. Caves and fissures open in the rock faces, and scattered thorn bushes, tamarisk and sparse grasses grow in the hollows. Under a wide sky the land is hard, empty and silent, with no settlement, road or city in view.

payload.title: Laws of worship, sacrifice, festivals and judges

aliases: the hill country of the Amorites
payload.name: Canaan
payload.note: The promised land of Israel as a whole, the land Yahweh gives to Abram's descendants, referred to in Genesis, Leviticus, Numbers, Deuteronomy, Judges and Hebrews alike; all six entries describe this same land.

stages.label: Canaan, the promised land

quotes.quote: Surely it flows with milk and honey, and this is its fruit.
Behold, Yahweh your God has set the land before you.
to the Western Sea
the land where you are traveling, all the land of Canaan, for an everlasting possession
seven nations greater and mightier than you

stages.text: Canaan: a fertile hill country between the Jordan river and the Western Sea, with terraced slopes, olive groves, vineyards heavy with grapes, wheat fields in the valleys, and wells beside walled mud-brick and stone towns on the hilltops. Scattered oaks and terebinths mark old sacred places, and herders' pastures roll toward the distant coast.

payload.title: Death of Saul and his sons on Gilboa

payload.name: Saul
payload.note: First king of Israel, son of Kish.

stages.label: Saul, first king of Israel

quotes.quote: Am I not a Benjamite, of the smallest of the tribes of Israel?
Saul disguised himself and put on other clothing
they found Saul and his three sons fallen on Mount Gilboa.

stages.text: Saul: a man in his forties, tall and broad-shouldered with a strong, weathered face, dark hair cut to the neck and a short, close beard. Skin olive-brown from sun. Dignified, brooding eyes. Signature outfit: a long undertunic of deep blue wool under a dark red royal cloak with a gold-bordered hem, a bronze-scaled leather belt and a plain sandal. Carries a royal spear of dark ash wood with a bronze head.

payload.name: Jonathan son of Saul
payload.note: Eldest son of King Saul and close friend of David; the same man across Samuel and Chronicles, killed with Saul on Gilboa. Distinguish from other Jonathans by being Saul's son and David's covenant friend.

stages.label: Jonathan son of Saul

quotes.quote: Jonathan stripped himself of the robe that was on him and gave it to David with his clothing, even including his sword, his bow, and his sash.
Jonathan the son of Saul said to the young man who bore his armor

stages.text: Jonathan son of Saul: a young man in his twenties, tall and lean, strong-shouldered from war; olive skin, dark close-cropped hair and a short trimmed beard; open, steady face with dark eyes. Signature outfit: a linen tunic in deep blue over which he wears a sleeveless bronze-scaled warrior's coat, with a crimson sash. Carries alone a curved bow of dark wood and a sword in a leather sheath.

payload.name: Mount Gilboa
payload.note: The battlefield where Saul and his sons fall, attested across Samuel and Chronicles as one mountain.

stages.label: Mount Gilboa

quotes.quote: fell down slain on Mount Gilboa.
You mountains of Gilboa, let there be no dew or rain on you, and no fields of offerings

stages.text: Mount Gilboa: a long, bare ridge of pale limestone and broken rock rising above the eastern Jezreel plain; sparse scrub of thorn and terebinth on the slopes, dry grass and stony ground near the crest, open fields of barley below, and a few weathered boulders along the ridge line.

payload.title: Walk as children of light
Against idols and prayer for mercy
Jehoahaz of Israel oppressed by Syria

payload.name: Jehoahaz of Israel
payload.note: Son of Jehu, king of Israel under Syrian oppression.

stages.label: King Jehoahaz of Israel

quotes.quote: Jehoahaz the son of Jehu began to reign over Israel in Samaria for seventeen years.

stages.text: Jehoahaz of Israel: man in his late thirties to forties; lean, strong build; olive-brown skin; dark hair and short trimmed beard streaked with grey at the temples; weathered, grave face with deep-set eyes and a furrowed brow. Signature outfit: a long undyed linen tunic with a deep indigo wool royal cloak fastened at the shoulder with a bronze clasp. Signature prop: a plain bronze-bound royal sword at his belt.

payload.name: Samaria (city)
payload.note: The northern kingdom's capital city, the hill of Samaria founded by Omri, besieged and fallen as described in Kings, Chronicles, Amos and Micah; foreign peoples are settled in the city in Ezra 4:10, and Philip preaches in the city in Acts. Distinct from the wider region and from Sychar.

stages.label: Samaria, hill capital

quotes.quote: He bought the hill Samaria of Shemer for two talents of silver; and he built on the hill
He raised up an altar for Baal in the house of Baal, which he had built in Samaria.
in an open place at the entrance of the gate of Samaria
They washed the chariot by the pool of Samaria
the city of Samaria, and in the rest of the country beyond the River

stages.text: Samaria: a broad, steep hill rising alone out of the central hill country, its slopes terraced with olive and vine. Walls of dressed limestone ring the crown, with a gate opening onto an open place by the entrance. Within stand a royal palace of cut stone and cedar beams, a house of Baal with an altar, and a pool at the foot of the hill.

payload.title: Curses and expulsion from the garden

payload.name: Adam
payload.note: The first man formed from dust in Eden, husband of Eve and father of Cain, Abel and Seth; the Genesis narrative figure, joined by the 1 Corinthians and 1 Timothy references to the same first man.

stages.label: Adam

quotes.quote: there he put the man whom he had formed
to cultivate and keep it
Yahweh God made garments of animal skins for Adam and for his wife, and clothed them.
All the days that Adam lived were nine hundred thirty years, then he died.

stages.text: Adam: a full-grown man in early middle age, sturdy and weathered from labour in the ground; broad shoulders, lean strong arms, dark brown skin darkened by sun; short dark curly hair and a close-cut beard; calm, grave face with deep-set eyes. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen wrap over one shoulder, later a simple garment of tawny animal skin; sandals of leather. No signature props, though he is often shown with a hoe or digging tool.

payload.name: Eve
payload.note: The first woman in Genesis, made from Adam's rib and deceived by the serpent; the other two entries (2 Corinthians 11:3 and 1 Timothy 2:14) refer back to this same Eve.

stages.label: Eve

quotes.quote: she would be the mother of all the living

stages.text: Eve: a woman in early adulthood, slender and strong, with a grounded, unhurried bearing. Warm olive-brown skin, dark eyes, long black hair bound back with a linen band. Her face is open and calm, with a serious, dignified expression. Signature outfit: a simple undyed linen wrap over one shoulder, falling to the knee, in ochre and sand tones. Carries no props alone.

payload.name: the serpent of Eden
payload.note: The subtle serpent of the garden who deceives Eve and is cursed in Genesis; the Corinthians reference points back to this same serpent.

stages.label: The serpent of Eden

quotes.quote: Now the serpent was more subtle than any animal of the field which Yahweh God had made.
you are cursed above all livestock, and above every animal of the field. You shall go on your belly and you shall eat dust all the days of your life.

stages.text: The serpent of Eden: an adult serpent of the field, long and sinuous, its body sleek and scaled in dull olive and dark ochre banded with pale bone-yellow, with a broad flattened head and cold, watchful eyes. Before the curse it is upright-bodied, slender and graceful, showing it was more subtle than the animals of the field; afterward it lies low, dusty, and close to the ground.

payload.name: Garden of Eden
payload.note: The garden planted by Yahweh God in Genesis, with the tree of life and forbidden tree; distinct from the garden in Song of Solomon and the garden across the Kidron.

stages.label: Garden of Eden

quotes.quote: Yahweh God planted a garden eastward, in Eden
including the tree of life in the middle of the garden and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil
A river went out of Eden to water the garden; and from there it was parted, and became the source of four rivers.
he placed cherubim at the east of the garden of Eden, and a flaming sword which turned every way

stages.text: Garden of Eden: a well-watered garden planted eastward in Eden, lush with pleasant trees bearing good fruit, the tree of life and the tree of knowledge standing in its middle. A single river issues from Eden, parting into four streams that water the ground. Soft green grass and fertile dark soil, with reeds along the banks. At the eastern edge, a boundary of cherubim and a flaming sword.

payload.title: Parable of the unforgiving servant

payload.name: Simon Peter
payload.note: The fisherman apostle, first-called disciple and leader of the twelve, who appears in the Gospels, Acts, Galatians and both letters of Peter; all entries here are the same individual, distinguished only by role and portrayal.

stages.label: Simon Peter

quotes.quote: Simon, who is called Peter, and Andrew, his brother, casting a net into the sea; for they were fishermen.
You are Simon the son of Jonah. You shall be called Cephas

stages.text: Simon Peter: a sturdy man in his thirties, broad-shouldered from hauling nets, weathered brown skin from sun on the Sea of Galilee, short dark curly hair and a full beard flecked with grey. Plain undyed tunic of natural linen under a rough brown wool cloak. Signature props: a coiled fishing net over one shoulder and a wooden fishing staff.

payload.title: Returnees to Jerusalem; gatekeepers and temple servants
Vision of the great prostitute

aliases: one of the seven angels with the bowls
the mighty angel with the little book
the angel of the abyss who speaks
payload.name: The angel who shows John
payload.note: The interpreting guide angel in Revelation who carries John in the Spirit and shows him visions; a shared role across several angels, treated as one guide figure.

stages.label: The angel who shows John
stages.text: The angel who shows John: a tall, luminous heavenly being of indeterminate age, grave and ageless; a robe of white linen with gold at the breast, a rainbow arching over the head like a crown of light, feet like pillars of fire, face shining bright as the sun, a voice like many waters; carries a small open scroll or little book in one hand.

payload.name: John the seer (Revelation)
payload.note: Author and visionary on Patmos who receives and records the revelation; the narrator of Revelation, distinct from other Johns.

stages.label: John the seer

quotes.quote: to his servant, John
I John, your brother and partner with you in the oppression

stages.text: John the seer: man of about sixty, of middle height and spare build, weathered olive skin from exile by the sea, short greying hair and a close grey beard, lined brow and steady dark eyes. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic of ochre-brown under a rough dark brown wool mantle. He carries a worn wooden staff and a small scroll case.

aliases: the woman in purple and scarlet
payload.name: The great prostitute (Babylon the great)
payload.note: Woman seated on the scarlet beast, named Babylon the great, who rules over kings in Revelation; the only such figure in the group.

stages.label: The great prostitute (Babylon the great)

quotes.quote: the judgment of the great prostitute who sits on many waters
MYSTERY, BABYLON THE GREAT, THE MOTHER OF THE PROSTITUTES AND OF THE ABOMINATIONS OF THE EARTH.
she who was dressed in fine linen, purple, and scarlet, and decked with gold and precious stones and pearls!

stages.text: The great prostitute, Babylon the great: a woman of mature age, about forty, with a regal, full figure and warm olive skin. Dark hair is piled high and crowned with gold and pearls. Her face is proud and composed, with heavy-lidded eyes and a firm mouth. Her signature garment is a gown of fine linen in deep purple and scarlet, richly embroidered and decked with gold, precious stones and pearls. On her forehead is a name in gold letters. She carries a golden cup.

payload.name: The wilderness (Revelation)
payload.note: The desert where the woman flees from the dragon and where the angel carries John in the Spirit.

stages.label: The wilderness

quotes.quote: the wilderness, where she has a place prepared by God
that she might fly into the wilderness to her place

stages.text: The wilderness: a wide, sun-scorched desert of pale sand and sun-cracked clay, rising into low, rust-coloured rocky ridges. Scattered thornbush, dry scrub and a few hardy palms mark old springs. Far off stands a stony outcrop, and the horizon shimmers in heat.

payload.title: Judgment on the corrupt rulers
Redemption of a sold Israelite servant
Census and pestilence

payload.name: Joab
payload.note: Son of Zeruiah and David's army commander, who kills Abner, Absalom and Amasa and leads the Ammonite campaign; distinguish from other Joabs by his role as David's commander in the army.

stages.label: Joab, captain of David's army

quotes.quote: Joab was clothed in his apparel of war that he had put on, and on it was a sash with a sword fastened on his waist in its sheath
He took three darts in his hand and thrust them through Absalom’s heart
Ten young men who bore Joab’s armor surrounded and struck Absalom

stages.text: Joab: a man in his middle years, around forty to fifty, of strong, weathered build with broad shoulders and a soldier's stance. Skin olive-brown and sun-browned. Dark hair cropped short at the neck, with a close-trimmed beard streaked with grey at the chin. Hard, watchful face with a broken nose. Signature outfit: a bronze-scaled or leather-plated military coat over a dark undertunic, with a deep red-brown war sash at the waist. Carries a sword in a plain sheath and three darts in hand.

payload.name: Gad the prophet
payload.note: Prophet and seer at David's court, advising David in 1 Samuel and bringing the choice of three punishments after the census in 2 Samuel and 1 Chronicles; identified by his role with David.

stages.label: Gad the prophet

quotes.quote: The prophet Gad said to David, “Don’t stay in the stronghold.
Yahweh’s word came to the prophet Gad, David’s seer

stages.text: Gad the prophet: man in middle age, lean and upright; olive skin; short greying beard, hair cropped at the neck; deep-set, steady eyes and a weathered, reserved face. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic under a dark brown wool cloak, the cloak in earthen umber. Carries a shepherd's staff of dark almond wood.

payload.title: Priests and Levites of earlier generations
Abram and Lot separate

aliases: Abraham the father of many nations
payload.name: Abram
payload.note: Son of Terah from Ur, called to Canaan and renamed Abraham; the same patriarch as Galatians' Abraham, so both entries form one cluster.

stages.label: Abram / Abraham

quotes.quote: Abram was seventy-five years old when he departed from Haran.
Abraham was one hundred years old when his son, Isaac, was born to him.
Abraham gave up his spirit, and died at a good old age, an old man, and full of years
Lot went with him.

stages.text: Abram, later Abraham: an elderly man of seventy-five to one hundred years and beyond; lean, weathered build from years of travel; dark skin tanned by desert sun; short greying beard and hair; deep-set, steady eyes and lined face. Signature outfit: a plain undyed wool wrap over a earth-brown linen tunic, leather sandals. Signature prop: a long wooden herder's staff.

payload.title: Sins that separate from God and the coming redeemer
Oracle against Babylon and the scroll

payload.name: Seraiah son of Neriah
payload.note: Quartermaster, son of Neriah, who carries Jeremiah's prophecy against Babylon to Babylon and reads it there (ch. 51); not the chief priest.

stages.label: Seraiah son of Neriah
stages.text: Seraiah son of Neriah: man in his forties, sturdy and steady in build, with olive-brown skin, short dark hair and a close-cut beard touched with grey at the chin. Deep-set, careful eyes and a grave, dignified face. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic under a dark indigo wool cloak fastened at the shoulder. Carries a clay-sealed scroll case of leather.

payload.title: Cornelius's vision and his messengers

payload.name: Cornelius
payload.note: Devout Roman centurion of Caesarea whose household receives the Holy Spirit in Acts 10.

stages.label: Cornelius, the centurion

quotes.quote: Now there was a certain man in Caesarea, Cornelius by name, a centurion of what was called the Italian Regiment,
a righteous man and one who fears God, and well spoken of by all the nation of the Jews

stages.text: Cornelius: a man of about fifty, middle height and sturdy build, with a weathered olive-brown skin, short greying dark hair, and a close-cut beard. Lined, steady, dignified face. Wears a Roman centurion's bronze-muscled cuirass over a red-brown tunic, with a dark red military cloak and leather sandals. Carries a plain short sword at the hip and a centurion's vine-staff.

payload.name: Cornelius's servants and soldier
payload.note: Two household servants and a devout soldier sent by Cornelius to fetch Peter.

stages.label: Cornelius's servants and soldier

quotes.quote: Cornelius called two of his household servants and a devout soldier of those who waited on him continually.

stages.text: Cornelius's servants and soldier: men of about thirty to forty; sturdy, unhurried build; olive-brown skin of Mediterranean complexion; short dark hair and a close-trimmed beard; calm, attentive faces. Servants wear a plain undyed linen tunic with a belted woollen cloak in ochre. The soldier wears a short Roman tunic in dark red with leather straps and a bronze-studded belt. Props: a leather pouch for the messenger's travel.

payload.name: an angel of the Lord
payload.note: Heavenly messenger of the Lord who appears in dreams and at key moments; the same angelic messenger role across Matthew and Acts, distinguished only by the episode, not by a separate identity.

stages.label: An angel of the Lord

quotes.quote: an angel of the Lord stood by him, and a light shone in the cell
saw his face like it was the face of an angel
an angel of the Lord descended from the sky

stages.text: An angel of the Lord: appears youthful and ageless, of tall, strong, well-proportioned build; skin fair and luminous; short light-brown hair; calm, steady features with a radiance about the face and head. Wears a long white tunic belted at the waist and a pale cloak of heavy linen, the robe glowing faintly with light. Carries no props.

payload.title: Jerusalem as an unfaithful foundling wife
Taunt against the king of Babylon
Second tablets, the ark, and blessing or curse

payload.name: Mount Ebal and Mount Gerizim
payload.note: The twin mountains in Deuteronomy where blessings and curses are proclaimed; distinct from the Judges Mount Gerizim, which is the same mountain only by name and is kept apart as a separate setting of Jotham's parable.

stages.label: Mount Ebal and Mount Gerizim

quotes.quote: you shall set the blessing on Mount Gerizim, and the curse on Mount Ebal.
These shall stand on Mount Gerizim to bless the people
These shall stand on Mount Ebal for the curse

stages.text: Mount Ebal and Mount Gerizim: two bare limestone ridges of the central hill country rising opposite each other across a narrow valley. Terraced slopes of olive and fig, scrub of thyme and oak; on Ebal, a plain stone altar and great stones set upright and coated with white plaster, catching the light.

payload.title: The Levite's concubine at Gibeah

aliases: the husband of the murdered woman
the man from the hill country of Ephraim
payload.name: The Levite husband of the concubine
payload.note: Levite from the hill country of Ephraim whose concubine is abused and killed at Gibeah; he cuts her body into twelve pieces. Not the young Levite of Bethlehem who serves Micah.

stages.label: The Levite husband of the concubine

quotes.quote: The Levite, the husband of the woman who was murdered, answered

stages.text: The Levite husband of the concubine: a man in his thirties, lean and weathered by travel, with olive skin, short dark hair and a close-trimmed beard shot with grey at the chin. Calm, grave features and steady dark eyes. He wears a plain woven tunic of undyed wool in ochre-brown beneath a long cloak of dusty grey-blue wool. He carries a traveller's staff of dark wood and a leather bag at his hip.

payload.name: The Levite's concubine
payload.note: Concubine of the Levite from Bethlehem Judah, raped and killed at Gibeah in Judges; distinct from Manoah's wife.

stages.label: The Levite's concubine

quotes.quote: She brought him into her father’s house; and when the father of the young lady saw him, he rejoiced to meet him.
the woman his concubine had fallen down at the door of the house, with her hands on the threshold.

stages.text: The Levite's concubine: a young woman in her late teens, slender, of modest height, olive-brown skin, dark hair bound back and covered with a linen veil. Plain woven tunic of undyed wool with a dull red border and a long cloak of rust-brown wool. Simple features, dignified and quiet, with a gentle face. No jewellery beyond a bronze ring.

payload.name: Men of Gibeah
payload.note: The wicked fellows of Gibeah, Benjamites who abuse the Levite's concubine to death; distinct from the Philistines and the tribe of Ephraim.

stages.label: Men of Gibeah

quotes.quote: certain wicked fellows, surrounded the house, beating at the door
They surrounded the Benjamites, chased them, and trod them down

stages.text: Men of Gibeah: adult men of mixed middle age, lean and sun-weathered from village and field life; medium to strong build; warm olive-brown skin; short dark hair and close-cropped beards; hard, set faces with heavy brows. Signature outfit: a woven undyed wool tunic with a rust-brown cloak thrown over the shoulders. Signature prop: a plain wooden cudgel carried at the belt.

payload.name: Bethlehem Judah
payload.note: The one town of Bethlehem in Judah, home of the Levite, Elimelech's family, Jesse and David; the same place across Judges, Ruth and 1 Samuel.

stages.label: Bethlehem Judah

quotes.quote: There was a young man out of Bethlehem Judah, of the family of Judah, who was a Levite; and he lived there.
All the people who were in the gate, and the elders, said
They came to Bethlehem in the beginning of barley harvest.
David went back and forth from Saul to feed his father’s sheep at Bethlehem.

stages.text: Bethlehem Judah: a walled hill town on a limestone ridge in the hill country of Judah, flat-roofed stone and mud-brick houses climbing terraced slopes, a city gate of heavy timber and stone where elders sit, olive groves and vineyards on the terraces, barley fields in the valley below, and a well outside the walls.

payload.name: Gibeah of Benjamin (Judges)
payload.note: The Benjamite city where the Levite's concubine is abused and killed and that is the scene of the war against Benjamin in Judges; distinguish from Saul's Gibeah in 1 Samuel by the Judges events of the concubine and the war.

stages.label: Gibeah of Benjamin

quotes.quote: the sun went down on them near Gibeah, which belongs to Benjamin
He went in, and sat down in the street of the city
The children of Israel rose up in the morning and encamped against Gibeah.

stages.text: Gibeah of Benjamin: a fortified hill town of the Benjamite highlands, set on a rocky ridge with terraced slopes. Low houses of mud brick and stone stand close together along a narrow street, flat roofs, and a city wall with a gate. Olive trees, vines and scrub grow on the slopes, with open fields and highways running out of the town.

payload.name: Jebus (Jebusite city before its capture)
payload.note: The earlier name of the same city while held by the Jebusites, before David took it; distinguished by the Jebusite occupation context in the judges entries.

stages.label: Jebus, Jebusite city on the hill

quotes.quote: The children of Judah fought against Jerusalem, took it, struck it with the edge of the sword, and set the city on fire.
the Jebusites dwell with the children of Benjamin in Jerusalem to this day.
he rose up and went near Jebus (also called Jerusalem).

stages.text: Jebus: a fortified hill town on a rocky ridge of limestone, with high stone walls of rough-hewn blocks and a strong citadel on the summit; flat-roofed houses of mud brick and stone terraced down the slopes; olive trees and terraced vineyards in the valleys below, a spring-fed water channel at the foot of the hill; a gate tower of weathered stone with dark timber doors.

payload.clothing: Woven tunics and wool cloaks, travel-worn; dark mourning garments and head coverings
payload.light: Dim lamplight and moonlight in the house; cool grey dawn light on the hills at the section's end
payload.place: Gibeah of Benjamin, a hill town of stone houses and an open threshing ground at its edge, with a distant view toward Jebus on the ridge
payload.timeOfDay: Night turning toward dawn across the section
payload.weather: Still, dry night air with low haze over the hills

payload.title: David rescues Keilah

payload.name: Men of Keilah
payload.note: Townsfolk of Keilah whom David rescues from the Philistines.

stages.label: Men of Keilah

quotes.quote: So David saved the inhabitants of Keilah.

stages.text: Men of Keilah: adult townsmen, mid-thirties to fifties; sturdy, weathered build from farm and field labour; olive-brown skin; short dark beard and cropped hair; lined, steady faces. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic with a rough brown woollen cloak in earth tones; carry a wooden staff or a simple iron-bladed spear and a round shield.

aliases: the priest with the ephod who flees to David
payload.name: Abiathar
payload.note: Son of Ahimelech who flees to David with the ephod.

stages.label: Abiathar

quotes.quote: he came down with an ephod in his hand.
One of the sons of Ahimelech the son of Ahitub, named Abiathar, escaped and fled after David.

stages.text: Abiathar: a man in his thirties, lean and sturdy from years of flight in the wilderness. Olive-brown skin, close-cropped dark hair and a short trimmed beard greying faintly at the chin. Calm, grave, watchful eyes and a weathered brow. Wears a plain undyed linen priestly tunic under a dark blue woollen cloak. Carries the linen ephod folded over his arm or shoulder.

payload.name: Keilah
payload.note: Town David saves from the Philistines.

stages.label: Keilah

quotes.quote: the Philistines are fighting against Keilah, and are robbing the threshing floors
he is shut in by entering into a town that has gates and bars

stages.text: Keilah: a walled hill-town in the Judean lowlands, built of rough-hewn limestone and mud brick with flat roofs and a stone city gate barred with heavy timber. Terraced threshing floors of packed earth lie just outside the walls, with low olive trees and wild terebinth on the slopes, and dry grass and stubble on the valley floor.

payload.title: Oracles against Ammon, Edom, Damascus, Kedar, Elam
Healing the withered hand

payload.name: the scribes
payload.note: Teachers of the law who question and oppose Jesus in Matthew and Luke; the Matthew and Luke entries describe the same scribal opposition and are joined.

stages.label: the scribes

quotes.quote: Beware of those scribes who like to walk in long robes
The scribes and the Pharisees sit on Moses’ seat.

stages.text: the scribes: men of middle to advanced age, lean and upright, of Judean build; olive skin, dark close-cropped or short-bearded hair, lined faces; a typical member wears a long undyed linen tunic under a dark wool cloak with long fringed tassels at the hem and phylacteries bound on the brow and left arm; sober dark blue and brown tones; often carries a small rolled scroll of the law.

payload.title: Yahweh's answer to the rebels and the faithful
Catalogue of the journeys

payload.name: The plains of Moab (Numbers)
payload.note: The camp across the Jordan from Jericho, also called Shittim, where the second census, Balaam's oracles and the Baal Peor apostasy take place; distinguish from the Deuteronomy camp by the Numbers events and the Shittim/Jericho alias.

stages.label: The plains of Moab (Numbers)

quotes.quote: The children of Israel traveled, and encamped in the plains of Moab beyond the Jordan at Jericho.
They traveled from the mountains of Abarim, and encamped in the plains of Moab by the Jordan at Jericho.
Israel stayed in Shittim;

stages.text: The plains of Moab: a broad, low, level tract of grey-green steppe east of the Jordan opposite Jericho, cut by the river's dense tamarisk and reed belt. Acacia (Shittim) groves and scrub grow on the plain; distant bluffs of the Abarim range rise eastward, and the walled city of Jericho glimmers across the river to the west. Scattered stone and mud-brick settlement walls, low tents of black goat hair, and open cairns mark the land.

payload.title: Ezra's prayer of confession
Gideon pursues Zebah and Zalmunna

payload.name: Gideon
payload.note: Manassite judge called by Yahweh's angel, also called Jerubbaal and son of Joash.

stages.label: Gideon

quotes.quote: His son Gideon was beating out wheat in the wine press
you mighty man of valor!

stages.text: Gideon: a man in his thirties, of lean, sturdy build with weathered brown skin from threshing and field labour. Dark brown hair falls to his shoulders, with a short trimmed beard. Steady, deep-set eyes and a broad, serious face. He wears a plain undyed woven linen tunic belted at the waist under a rust-brown wool cloak. Carries a simple wooden threshing staff or a plain sword.

payload.name: Tribe of Ephraim (men of Ephraim)
payload.note: The Israelite tribe in the judges' era that quarrels with Gideon and Jephthah; distinct from the person and from the northern kingdom.

stages.label: Men of Ephraim

quotes.quote: The men of Ephraim were gathered together, and passed northward
At that time, forty-two thousand of Ephraim fell.

stages.text: Men of Ephraim: adult men, late twenties to forties; sturdy, weathered build; olive-brown skin; dark hair worn to the shoulder and short, close-trimmed beards; strong brows and steady eyes. Signature dress: a dark-blue woven wool tunic belted at the waist under a rust-brown cloak. Carry a round leather shield and a short spear.

payload.name: Midianites of Judges
payload.note: Raiding peoples in Judges who oppress Israel for seven years and are defeated by Gideon's three hundred; distinguished by the Gideon context and the Zebah and Zalmunna pursuit.

stages.label: Midianites of Judges

quotes.quote: Yahweh delivered them into the hand of Midian seven years.
lay along in the valley like locusts for multitude; and their camels were without number

stages.text: Midianites of Judges: adult men, ages twenty to forty; lean, weathered desert build; olive-bronze skin; dark hair bound back with a cord, short beards; hard, watchful faces. Signature outfit: a long undyed wool robe in ochre and dun, belted at the waist, with a dark-brown cloak against the wind. Signature props: a curved sword and a leather sling at the belt.

payload.name: Succoth (town of Gideon, Judges)
payload.note: The town whose elders refused bread to Gideon's pursuing men and were punished with thorns; distinguish from the Genesis and Exodus places by its judicial-military narrative.

stages.label: Succoth

quotes.quote: He said to the men of Succoth, “Please give loaves of bread to the people who follow me
He took the elders of the city, and thorns of the wilderness and briers, and with them he taught the men of Succoth.

stages.text: Succoth: a walled settlement on a low rise in the Jordan valley east of the river; mud-brick houses with flat roofs, a fortified gate of timber and stone, and a central open square worn bare by use; thorn scrub, wild briers and tamarisk grow along the wadi edges and the desert margin beyond the fields; scattered terraced grain plots, olive and fig trees.

payload.name: Penuel
payload.note: Town whose tower Gideon breaks down.

stages.label: Penuel

quotes.quote: When I come again in peace, I will break down this tower.
He broke down the tower of Penuel, and killed the men of the city.

stages.text: Penuel: a fortified town on a rocky rise beside the Jabbok ford in Gilead; stone-footed walls of mud brick above, a tall square watchtower of heavy stone and brick at its gate, flat-roofed houses packed inside, scrubby terebinth and tamarisk along the riverbank, dry grassland beyond.

payload.name: Karkor
payload.note: Place where Zebah and Zalmunna are captured.

stages.label: Karkor

quotes.quote: Now Zebah and Zalmunna were in Karkor, and their armies with them, about fifteen thousand men

stages.text: Karkor: a wide, dry hollow in the arid eastern desert beyond the Jordan, floored with pale sand and cracked clay; low sun-bleached rock ridges rise on three sides, with scattered tamarisk and thorn scrub clinging to the wadi banks. Simple encampment ground of woven black goat-hair tents and stone-ringed hearths; a few crumbling mudbrick walls of an old caravan stop mark the edge of the hollow.

payload.title: The officers report; Nicodemus speaks

aliases: the soldiers sent to arrest him
payload.name: the temple officers
payload.note: Officers sent by the chief priests and Pharisees to arrest Jesus, who return impressed by his words; a collective group of temple police, distinct from the elders of Deuteronomy.

stages.label: the temple officers

quotes.quote: The officers therefore came to the chief priests and Pharisees
the detachment, the commanding officer, and the officers of the Jews seized Jesus and bound him
Now the servants and the officers were standing there, having made a fire of coals, for it was cold.

stages.text: the temple officers: men in their late twenties to middle age; sturdy, practical build; olive-brown skin; short dark hair and close-trimmed beard; steady, watchful face with a dignified, unhurried bearing. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic with a deep-blue wool cloak pinned at the shoulder. Signature prop: a short wooden staff of office.

aliases: a Pharisee who came by night
payload.name: Nicodemus
payload.note: Pharisee and ruler of the Jews who visits Jesus by night, defends him, and helps bury him; appears in the John sections on his night visit, the officers' report, his speech, and the garden tomb burial.

stages.label: Nicodemus, Pharisee and ruler of the Jews

quotes.quote: a man of the Pharisees named Nicodemus, a ruler of the Jews.

stages.text: Nicodemus: a man of mature years, late fifties, lean and dignified; olive skin weathered by desert sun; short greying beard trimmed close and a lined, thoughtful face. Dark brown eyes. He wears a long undertunic of undyed linen under a deep blue wool cloak with tasselled hem, marking his rank. He carries a small leather scroll case.

payload.name: the Jerusalem temple
payload.note: The single Jerusalem temple building across all five divisions (courts, porch and gates are parts of the same place), so every entry is one place.

stages.label: The Jerusalem temple

quotes.quote: Jesus entered into the temple of God and drove out all of those who sold and bought in the temple
The veil of the temple was torn in two from the top to the bottom.
the door of the temple which is called Beautiful
how it was decorated with beautiful stones and gifts
His disciples came to him to show him the buildings of the temple.

stages.text: The Jerusalem temple: a vast complex of white limestone and gleaming gold on a raised stone platform atop Mount Moriah. Wide colonnaded courts, a tall sanctuary house with a gilded roof, a great curtained veil within, a treasury chamber, and a Beautiful Gate of bronze. Olive trees and cedar frame the courts.
